Round-two review complete. Writing the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round two. Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** as Kethra Anvilmark, same as round one (`fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:388` — top Forge rung, not the Sol rung the charter flags for reward-hacking). The round-one blocker is fixed, in exactly the shape the Mayor's dispatch specified, and nothing else moved: `af1d2da` touches two files, `test/shell.test.ts` and a new handoff. `bin/fort-init` and `templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh` are byte-identical to the round-one commit I already found correct. Round discipline applies: only regressions and unfixed round-one blockers could block here, and there are none of either.

**The round-one blocker is closed.** The founding smoke is now gated on `test.skipIf(!foundingSmokeToolsAvailable)` (`test/shell.test.ts:155`), where the gate is a single `sh -c 'command -v bd >/dev/null && command -v jq >/dev/null'` under try/catch (`:26-39`). `execFileSync` throws on nonzero exit; POSIX `command -v` exits nonzero on a missing name; the `&&` short-circuits on the first miss. Every failure direction — bd missing, jq missing, `sh` itself unreachable — lands on `false`, which skips. That is the safe direction for a guard whose job is to keep the verifier green. `test/shell.test.ts` is now the only place in the suite that reaches for `bd` at all (`test/digest.test.ts:80` stubs it on PATH, `src/readers/beads.ts` tolerates its absence), so the suite's deliberate bd-hermeticity is restored rather than merely patched around.

The gate requires **both** tools, which is what makes it robust independent of the one thing I flagged as uncertain in round one. I said then that the bd half of my CI reasoning was near-certain and the jq half less so; with an `&&` gate, jq's presence on the runner no longer matters. Missing bd alone suffices to skip. My round-one requirement — *`fort/scripts/verify.sh` must exit 0 in an environment with Node + ShellCheck and nothing else* — is met.

**Gates.** Human gate 1 not tripped: the only `fort/` path touched is `fort/handoffs/`, a record. Gate 2 (`.env*`) untouched. Gate 3 not tripped by a merge. No mandatory-ESCALATE case applies.

---

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking, new) The coverage is now conditional, and nothing tells anyone when it stops running.** This is the honest cost of option (a), and it is worth naming because it is the same defect class the bead exists to kill, one ring further out: a gate that is green because it did not run. Today the smoke executes on Justin's machine (bd at `/home/justin/.local/bin/bd`, jq at `/usr/bin/jq`) and skips in CI; if bd ever leaves that machine, the fort's only founding smoke goes quiet and every lane reports green. The fix is already scoped — the Mayor's option-(b) bead (install bd+jq in `ci.yml`) makes the skip unreachable and dissolves the concern entirely. My ask is only that the two be linked, so option (b) is understood as closing this and not merely as nice-to-have. One thing for whoever takes it: `bin/fort-init:13` runs `bd init` and `:20-23` four `bd config set` calls plus `bd export`; whether those succeed unattended on a fresh runner with no bd state is unverified, so treat (b) as real work rather than a one-line apt step.

**2. (non-blocking, nit) The skip reason rides in the test name, so it prints even when the test runs.** `test/shell.test.ts:156` interpolates `foundingSmokeSkipReason` into the title, yielding `founds a fort whose shipped verifier passes (founding smoke requires bd+jq; CI install step tracked separately)` on every green run. Vitest's `skipIf` has no reason field, so name-embedding is the standard workaround and I would not change it for its own sake — but the Mayor asked for a *skip* message and this is a *test* message. Noted so nobody later reads it as a description of what the test asserts. No bead needed.

**3. (non-blocking, carried) Round-one findings 2-5 are still open and, as of this review, not yet filed.** I grepped `.beads/issues.jsonl` for a bead referencing `ajj` and found none. The Mayor's dispatch says they are being beaded, and deferring them was the correct call — I record only that the filing hadn't happened at review time, because standing order 5 makes the follow-up bead the thing that closes the loop, not the intention to file one. The four: the smoke asserts exit 0 and nothing about which steps ran (finding 2); `fort/scripts/lib/*.sh` is the same unmatched-glob trap one level down, wanting `nullglob` or `find -exec` (finding 3); `FORT_REGISTRY` is undocumented in `bin/fort-init`'s usage header, in `fort/remember.md`, and in the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md block fort-init writes into every founded repo (finding 4); and `fortkit-vlj` should record that part of its scope now lives at `test/shell.test.ts:154` (finding 5).

**4. (non-blocking, record accuracy) The round-two handoff repeats round one's model label and its "no open risks" line.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-round-2.md` again says "Model: GPT-5 Codex", which is not a rung on the charter's Forge ladder and does not disambiguate Terra from Sol; the authoritative event says `gpt-5.6-terra`, so the record of record is right and only the handoff is loose. Its "Open risks" line is better than round one's — it names the deferred CI install — though it frames the skip purely as tracked work rather than as conditional coverage (finding 1). One imprecision worth a correction rather than a bead: it calls the reason string a "skipped-test label", when the string is present in the test name whether or not the test skips. Every checkable factual claim in it reproduced. Corrections append, never edit (order 7).

**5. (non-blocking, merge mechanics — carried from round one, still live).** `bead/ajj` is **3 commits behind main** (`rev-list --left-right --count` → `3 3`). Two-dot `git diff main..bead/ajj` therefore still shows the fci.5 sprite-pathing work as deletions; the real change set is `git diff main...bead/ajj`, five files. Main's side of the divergence is `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`, `src/colony-page.ts`, `test/world.test.ts` — **disjoint** from this bead's five, so the merge should be textually clean. Merge `--no-ff` from main; do not rebase main onto the branch, do not reset. Main's checkout is still dirty with pre-existing bd/config churn (`M .beads/interactions.jsonl`, `M .beads/issues.jsonl`, `?? .claude/.proven-config-version`, `?? .claude/proven-config.json`) — unrelated to this diff, but it will muddy a `git status` check at merge time.

---

### Verified independently

- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` then `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in the scratch copy: **green** — Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (46 files), **70/70 Vitest**, ShellCheck silent. Identical to round one; no regression, and no test lost.

- `test/shell.test.ts` is the sole remaining bd consumer in the suite (grep across `test/`); `test/digest.test.ts:78-80` stubs bd on PATH.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:23-29` installs **only** ShellCheck before running `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — the condition that made round one's finding blocking, unchanged, and now harmless.
- `git diff main...bead/ajj -- bin/fort-init templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh`: the round-one fix is unchanged — the template drops only `bin/fort-init` from its ShellCheck targets, and the factory's own `fort/scripts/verify.sh:66` still covers `bin/fort-init`, `bin/regent`, `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh`, and `civ/scripts/*.sh`. No ShellCheck coverage lost in fortkit itself.
- `af1d2da` is path-scoped to two files, no `.beads`/lockfile churn (order 4). Candidate worktree clean at the branch tip; scratch copy confirmed at the round-two state.
- Event stream: `bead.claimed` / `session.start` (gpt-5.6-terra) / `work.begun` / `work.ended` / `session.end` exit 0, all correctly targeted at `fortkit-ajj`; the Mayor's emit recipe with the required `-t` value was followed.
- No `ajj` follow-up beads present in `.beads/issues.jsonl` at review time (finding 3).

### Taken on faith

- **The negative-PATH run — I could not reproduce it.** The Forge reports that with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, `npx vitest run test/shell.test.ts` passes with 6 tests and one skip. My seat denied every route to a modified PATH (three attempts: an `env` prefix, an `env` invocation, and a Node child-process spawn with an overridden `PATH`), and it denied writing a wrapper script into the scratch copy. That is the read-only construction working as designed, not a defect. What I can say is that the claim is coherent with this machine's actual layout — `which -a` shows `node`, `npx` and `npm` in `/usr/bin` as well as under nvm, and `jq` at `/usr/bin/jq`, while `bd` exists **only** at `/home/justin/.local/bin/bd`. So `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` does hide bd while keeping Node and jq, and the reported 6-plus-1 result is exactly what the gate predicts. I verified the gate by reading and verified the positive path by running it; the negative path rests on that reasoning plus the Forge's report.
- That the GitHub `ubuntu-24.04` runner ships no bd. As close to certain as an unobserved fact gets — Beads is Justin's own tooling under `~/.local/bin`, not a distro package — and the `&&` gate means jq's presence no longer matters either way.
- That `bd init` and `bd config set` confine their writes to the temp repo's `.beads/`. Unchanged from round one and still unverifiable from this seat; it now matters only on hosts where the smoke actually runs. comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
# Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Bead:** fortkit-fci.5 — L6: Sprite pathing. **Range reviewed:** `main..bead/fci.5` (commits `8d49b5a` implementation, `b64d285` handoff). **Model that produced the work:** self-reported "GPT-5 Codex, as Kethra Anvilmark (she/her)" in the handoff — a GPT-5-family Codex run, so I applied the heightened scrutiny the seat file calls for on that vendor, specifically hunting for weakened guards, narrowed verifiers, and deleted tests. I found what looked like exactly that, and it turned out not to be this diff's doing (finding 1). Round one.

Nothing here meets the blocking bar: the verifier reproduces green, every claim in the handoff checks out against the code, no gate-listed area is touched, and I found no correctness bug. Gate note: charter gate 1 names "`fort/` files, seat definitions, launchers, permission profiles" as the constitution. This branch touches `fort/handoffs/` only. I read routine records under `fort/handoffs/`, `fort/events/`, `fort/annals/` as ordinary seat output rather than constitution — the charter's own Memory section lists them as normal seat machinery, the mechanical read-only set is `.claude/`, `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, and the `fortkit-tmu` merge already on main carried a handoff append through Warden approval without escalation. So no mandatory ESCALATE. I state the reading explicitly because it is a judgment call.

---

## 1. The requested diff range shows reversions this branch did not make — **non-blocking**, but read it before merging

`git diff main..bead/fci.5` shows, on top of the pathing work, what look like four serious regressions: the empty-category guard removed from both `fort/scripts/emit.sh` and `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh`, `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh` dropped from the ShellCheck surface in `verify.sh`, the template emitter's whole test arm deleted from `test/shell.test.ts`, and the `expectNoEvents` directory assertion replaced with a hardcoded `events-2026-08-08.jsonl` filename check that would pass vacuously on any other date. That reads as textbook reward hacking.

It is not. Per-commit stats are conclusive: `8d49b5a` touches only `src/colony-page.ts` and `test/world.test.ts`; `b64d285` touches only `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`, 30 insertions, 0 deletions. The branch never touches those files. `main` has moved ahead by `7bad0fa` (merge of `bead/tmu`, "guards date-independent", Warden approved round 1), which *added* those hardenings. `bead/fci.5` was cut before it. The two-dot range renders main's newer work as deletions. A three-way merge takes main's side for all four files; nothing is reverted.

Recording this in full because a reviewer or a Mayor reading that range without checking per-commit scope would reasonably block, and the same stale-branch pattern will recur. This bears on threat 1 (agent accident): the failure mode is a correct change being reverted, or a false regression report going on the record. Worth a bead to have the launcher pass a three-dot range or the merge-base to the Warden.

## 2. The handoff file will conflict on merge, and the wrong resolution deletes a record — **non-blocking**

Main's tmu merge appended a `2026-08-07T16:18-08:00` entry to the tail of `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`; this branch appends a `16:28:00-08:00` entry at the same tail. Main's merge commit already records `# Conflicts: fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md` once. Standing order 7 is append-only: the resolution must keep **both** entries, tmu's first, not take-ours or take-theirs. Flagging because the naive resolution produces precisely the deletion that finding 1's diff appears to show.

## 3. The animation loop closes over a stale projection — **non-blocking**

`requestAnimation(projection)` captures the projection argument, and the `requestAnimationFrame` callback re-enters `render(projection)` with that captured value, re-scheduling itself for as long as a motion is active. During a walk the rAF chain therefore repaints a projection up to 1.2 s old. Two consequences: a 5 s poll landing mid-walk renders fresh data once and is then overwritten by the stale chain for the remainder of the motion (stale ticker text and detail panel); and if a second session transition lands within 1.2 s, the stale chain can re-detect the *previous* transition and briefly reverse the walk — which partly undoes the mid-walk handling the code comments at `src/colony-page.ts:445` were written to provide. Bounded at 1.2 s of cosmetic staleness in a decorative renderer, so not blocking. The clean fix is a module-level `latestProjection` that `render` writes and the rAF callback reads.

## 4. No test asserts an intermediate interpolated position — **non-blocking**

The new test in `test/world.test.ts` pins progress 0 (`departing` at the ambient coords with `idle: false`) and progress 1 (`atWorkshop` at 297,130; `atAmbient` away from it). Those two together are equally consistent with a 1.2 s *delayed teleport* — the lerp itself is unverified. Since "sprites visibly walk" is the headline acceptance criterion, an assertion at `t = 600` for the exact midpoint of the two endpoints is the one line that would actually pin it. Bead it.

## 5. Ambient placement is obtained via a synthetic citizen — **non-blocking**

`placementFor({ ...target.citizen, currentBead: null, session: null }, ...)` fabricates a citizen record to make `placementFor` take its ambient branch. It works, and it correctly honours the dispatch addendum by keeping `placementFor`/`occupantPosition` the single position source, but "construct a fake domain object to select a code path" is the kind of thing that reads as a trick to the next person. An `ambientPlacementFor(citizen, index, timestamp, seed)` helper that both callers use would say what it means. `currentBead: null` is also inert here — the ambient branch never reads it.

## 6. Walk speed varies with distance; labels go subpixel mid-walk — **non-blocking, cosmetic**

`walkingDurationMilliseconds` is a fixed 1.2 s regardless of path length, so a bed-to-adjacent-workshop hop crawls while a cross-map walk sprints. And interpolated `x`/`y` are fractional, so `fillText` renders the glyph and name at subpixel offsets during motion — slightly soft labels for 1.2 s. Both are taste calls; constant-speed (px/ms) with a floor, and rounding only the label coordinate, would address them if anyone cares.

## 7. "Works in replay" is verified structurally, not against a scrubber — **non-blocking**

No replay scrubber exists yet (`docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:82` still lists it as a v1 item). The acceptance criterion is met in the sense that matters — the function is timestamp- and seed-parameterized and the new test drives it entirely through explicit timestamps — but two things will need attention when the scrubber lands, and belong in that bead rather than this one: `render` calls `animatedCitizenPlacements(projection)` with no timestamp, so it always defaults to `Date.now()` and a scrubber cannot thread its clock through; and because `progress` is clamped at 0 and the completion check is `timestamp - startsAt >= duration`, a *backward* seek leaves a motion parked at progress 0 indefinitely until time advances forward again. I raise these as forward notes, not as imagined infrastructure failures under standing order 11.

## 8. Model attribution does not match a ladder rung — **non-blocking**

The handoff records "GPT-5 Codex". The charter's Forge ladder reads GPT-5.6 Terra → Sol → Sonnet 5 → Opus 5. The immediately preceding fci.4 entry uses the same "GPT-5 Codex" string, so this is an established naming habit rather than an off-ladder run, but the record does not let a stranger tell which rung was used. A one-time convention note in `fort/remember.md` would settle it.

## 9. Threat-model assessment — no finding

Against the charter's threats in priority order: **1, agent accident** — the only exposure is finding 1's misleading diff range, filed above. **2, prompt injection** — the diff adds no untrusted-input boundary; citizen names and bead ids reach the canvas through `fillText`, not markup, so no new injection surface. **3, supply chain** — no dependency change; `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched, satisfying the bead's "no new deps". **4, credential leakage** — nothing touches secrets or logging. No control is weakened by this diff. Nothing here requires the out-of-scope shell-access adversary to matter, and nothing here defends against one.

---

## Spec and dispatch conformance

- **Layout table as the single position source** (dispatch addendum, coordinating with fortkit-zkj): satisfied and verified. Every coordinate in the new code comes from `placementFor` → `occupantPosition`; the new code computes no coordinate of its own beyond lerping between two `placementFor` outputs. zkj's hit-box rework will land under it cleanly.
- **Hit boxes follow the sprite:** verified — `render` feeds the *animated* placements into the click hit test at `src/colony-page.ts:634`, so a walking citizen is clickable where they are drawn.
- **Spec:** `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:72` already specifies exactly this behaviour, including the "rendering may lag reality" clause. No spec update was owed, so standing order 3 is satisfied without a docs change.
- **Straight-line lerp** is within spec: the acceptance criterion asks for "path *endpoints* from the layout table", not obstacle-aware routing.
- **Ambient resumes after return:** verified by the `atAmbient` assertions and by the motion being deleted at completion so the sprite returns to plain `placementFor` output.

## What I verified independently

Ran the authoritative verifier in the scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-fci.5` after `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` (52 packages, lockfile-pinned): `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exited 0 with typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (46 files, no fixes), Vitest **67 tests across 9 files**, and ShellCheck all green — matching the handoff's claim exactly. Separately ran ShellCheck with main's *wider* surface (`templates/fort/scripts/*.sh` re-added) to confirm the post-merge verifier is also green: clean. Confirmed per-commit file scope with `git show --stat` on both commits, and confirmed main's divergence via `git log bead/fci.5..main`. Read the full implementation and traced the transition, mid-walk re-entry, completion, and roster-prune paths by hand. Confirmed no dependency changes from the diffstat. Confirmed the pre-existing `citizenPlacements` test still stands and the function is still exercised directly.

## What I took on faith

I did not open a browser: "sprites visibly walk" is judged from the code and the endpoint tests, not from observed pixels — which is exactly why finding 4 matters. I did not attempt the merge or its conflict resolution (zero write permissions), so finding 2 is predicted from the two commits' contents rather than executed. I did not query `bd` for bead state. I took the handoff's account of its own failed attempts (`npm ci` recovery, Biome formatting, the `packed-refs.lock` warning) as reported; the tree's green state is consistent with all three.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: verifier green (67 tests/9 files); pathing layout-sourced and correct; 8 non-blocking findings; branch stale vs main

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round one on substance. Two earlier Warden sessions on this bead (events 234–238, 2026-08-07) died at launch and recorded incidents with no verdict; the launcher behaved exactly as designed and neither is a prior round. Work produced by the Forge's top ladder rung: the event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra` (event 226); the handoff header says "GPT-5 Codex". I weighted for the reward-hacking watch on the GPT-5.x line and went looking specifically for tests that cannot fail — finding 7 is what that search turned up, and it is the only thing of that class in the diff.

Nothing here is blocking. The core is what the spec asked for: a genuinely pure, total, UTC-only function with no daemon, no state file, no model call, no new dependency, and no network. Gate 1 was honoured correctly and without prompting — no launcher was touched, and the launcher work is split into `fortkit-fci.6` (open, Overseer-owned, correctly scoped "do not alter ambient scheduling or read/write any state"). The only `fort/` path in the diff is `fort/handoffs/`, which is a seat's own write, not constitution. No gate-listed ESCALATE area is in range. Against the charter's threat model, this diff bears on none of 1–4: it adds one read-only file read and a pure computation.

## Findings

**1. Idle pursuits are deterministic but not flavoured — non-blocking.**
`src/ambient.ts:104-112` picks from the four-pastime table with `hash(identity + day + 3-hour block) % 4`. That is deterministic per citizen, but the distribution is uniform and identical for every citizen: over a week Kethra and Ilva each read, walk, fish and tinker in roughly equal measure. Their *sequences* differ; their *habits* do not. The spec (ambient-life.md:35) asks for "recognizable habits" and "personality flavor … from a per-citizen deterministic pick", and this bead's own description says "idle pursuits flavored per citizen". A per-citizen weighting over the table — a favourite drawn once from `hash(identity)`, then sampled against — would deliver it in a few lines. This is the largest gap between the diff and the bead text; it is not a correctness bug and the scaffold it lands on is the right one, so it is a bead, not a block.

**2. `--since` behaves as `--on` — non-blocking, but fix before fci.6 lands.**
`src/cli.ts:24-41` prints the entire UTC day containing the timestamp, so `--since 2026-08-07T22:00Z` prints from 00:00 that day — almost entirely *before* "since", and including hours in the future. The spec's stated use for the window is "integrate the function over the window since her last session" (ambient-life.md:26), which is precisely the query the launcher line in fci.6 will need. The handoff is honest about the behaviour ("prints the UTC day schedule containing the supplied timestamp"), so this is a naming/semantics divergence rather than a misrepresentation. Rename to `--on`, or make `--since` mean since — but decide before fci.6 builds on the surface, because after that it is a breaking change to a gate-1 file's caller.

**3. The fort marches in lockstep — non-blocking.**
Breakfast, lunch, dinner and the social window are byte-identical for every citizen (`src/ambient.ts:88-100`), with a code comment stating the choice deliberately. Only sleep is offset, into five half-hour buckets. The spec asked for windows that "deliberately overlap" so citizens meet — not for windows that are identical — and for the fort to "breathe rather than march in lockstep" (ambient-life.md:31,34). Co-presence and breathing are both obtainable: jitter arrival and departure per citizen around a guaranteed shared core. This will be visible the moment L4 renders the Tavern.

**4. The fort seed is derived from the current working directory — non-blocking.**
`src/cli.ts:12-22` regexes `./fort/charter.md` for the fort name and silently falls back to the literal string `"this fort"` on any failure. Run `fortkit ambient kethra` from `~` and you get a complete, plausible, *different* schedule with no indication anything is wrong — against a spec whose load-bearing consequence is "two viewers always agree" (ambient-life.md:24). The other subcommands already resolve forts through `~/.claude/civilization.json`; ambient should use the same source, or fail loudly. Compounding it: `activity()` accepts `fortSeed: string | number` and interpolates it into the identity, so `activity(c, t, "Manyhalls")` and `activity(c, t, fortSeedFor("Manyhalls"))` return different schedules. In a function whose contract is agreement between independent evaluators, that parameter should be `number` only.

**5. Unparseable timestamps become 1970 — non-blocking.** `millisecondsAt` (`src/ambient.ts:38-47`) returns `0` for anything `Date.parse` rejects. Totality is a spec requirement and the CLI validates first, so this is defensible, but a renderer evaluating client-side on a bad timestamp will draw a citizen doing something entirely plausible rather than showing a fault. This is the failure that renders beautifully. Throw, or document the epoch fallback as deliberate.

**6. `place` is untyped and its vocabulary exists nowhere — non-blocking.** `AmbientState.place` is `string` while `activity` is a proper union. `river` and `tinker-bench` appear in no layout table: the visualizer amendment's permanent-buildings table (fortress-visualizer.md:48-63) has no river, walls, or tinker bench, and `src/colony-page.ts:142-187` hardcodes GATE / TRADE DEPOT / ARCHIVE / DUNGEON with no Tavern or homes. The spec anticipated this loosely ("home:<citizen>, tavern, archive, walls, …") but fci.5 is blocked on this bead and must path between these places. Declare an `AmbientPlace` union before L4/L6 consume it, so a typo becomes a type error rather than a sprite standing in a void. (Noted in passing: `src/ambient.ts` imports nothing from node and is browser-clean, which is the right call given the renderer evaluates it client-side — but the fort's no-bundler page pattern inlines a single module, so L4 needs a plan for sharing it.)

**7. The DST test cannot fail — non-blocking, and the one I most want fixed.**
`test/ambient.test.ts:22-28` compares `2026-03-08T12:30:00-08:00` against `2026-03-08T20:30:00Z` and `12:30:00-07:00` against `19:30:00Z`. Those are the same instant written two ways, so both assertions reduce to `f(x) == f(x)`; the test passes for any implementation that is a pure function of the instant, including one reading host-local time — which is the exact failure a DST test exists to catch. It also never asserts the two states differ, and for `ilva` at 19:30Z and 20:30Z they don't (both fall in the social window). The bead's acceptance criterion "tested across day boundaries and DST" is therefore met only nominally. **I verified the underlying property holds anyway**: I re-ran the suite under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` and `TZ=America/Anchorage` and it stays green, because the sleep and co-presence tests do pin absolute UTC behaviour. So the guarantee is real; the test that claims to prove it doesn't. Replace it with a stubbed non-UTC `TZ` and an absolute expectation.

**8. The new CLI branch has no CLI-level test — non-blocking.** `test/cli.test.ts` already spawns `node src/cli.ts` via `execFileAsync` and asserts exit code 2 for `world` and `digest`. The handoff's stated reason for omitting an ambient equivalent is that `execFile` returned empty stdout for positional Node scripts — but the existing tests never read stdout, and the `ambient` validation expression (`src/cli.ts:29-34`, five conjuncts, one of them redundant) is testable by exit code in exactly the way the neighbours already are. The stated obstacle does not cover the omission.

**9. Record integrity: `work.ended` names a commit that no longer exists — non-blocking, but file the correction.**
Event 232 records `{"commit":"eeb8554"}`. The reflog shows `eeb8554` was then amended into the reviewed tip `c3b8b6c`, so the recorded hash resolves on no ref, and the traceability from the fort's event stream to the merged code is broken for this bead. The amend was not cosmetic: it changed product code, narrowing the sleep offset from `hash % 121` to `(hash % 5) * 30` — a real fix, since a sleep start at, say, 21:37 would have made `formatAmbientDay`'s 30-minute sampling render a schedule that disagreed with the function it renders. But the handoff's "verifier green" claim was written before that change. I do not call the claim false — I re-ran four of the five gates against the amended tip myself and they are green (see below). Standing order 7 makes the remedy an appended correction, not an edit: emit a corrected `work.ended` naming `c3b8b6c`, and adopt the practice that `work.ended` is emitted after the final commit, with any amend followed by a re-run and an appended event.

**10. "Sessions override everything" is unimplemented and unrecorded — non-blocking.** ambient-life.md:36 makes this part of the schedule; a pure stateless function cannot do it, so it belongs to the consumer, and deferring it is right. But nothing in the diff or the handoff records the deferral, and today `fortkit ambient kethra` will report her lunching at the Tavern while she is mid-session at the Forge. The header framing ("Ambient schedule for…") keeps that honest for now, and no renderer consumes it yet. Given `fortkit-wkf` (colony render honesty) landed on main three commits ago, I'd add the override requirement explicitly to `fortkit-fci.3` (L4) rather than leave it implied.

**11. Merge-time task for the Mayor — non-blocking.** `docs/specs/ambient-life.md` still reads "Status: approved direction, pre-implementation" and "v1 shape, tuned during implementation". The shape was tuned; the spec doesn't say how. Specs are the Mayor's to write, so the Forge was right not to touch it — but standing order 3 makes the update expected output of the cycle, not optional, and it should land with the merge.

**12. Handoff model naming — non-blocking, pre-existing.** The handoff says "GPT-5 Codex"; the event stream says `gpt-5.6-terra`. The event is authoritative and names a real ladder rung, so failover accounting is intact. Six existing handoffs use the same imprecise string, so this is fort-wide drift, not something this diff introduced.

## What I verified independently, and what I took on faith

Verified myself, in the scratch tree at `/tmp/warden-fci.4`:
- The scratch copies of `src/ambient.ts` and `src/cli.ts` are byte-identical to `bead/fci.4`, so I reviewed and tested the tip, not a stale copy.
- The branch is one commit (`c3b8b6c`) off `0dc02e8`, touching exactly four files; nothing in `fort/` except a handoff.
- `npm ci` from the committed lockfile (52 packages, no new dependency in `package.json`).
- `tsc --noEmit` against `tsconfig.json` — clean. `tsc --noEmit` against `tsconfig.browser.json` — clean.
- `vitest run` — 46 tests across 8 files, matching the handoff's claim exactly. Re-run under `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` and `TZ=America/Anchorage`: still 46/46.
- `shellcheck -x fort/scripts/verify.sh` — clean (no shell script is changed by this diff).
- `main` has advanced three commits since the branch point, but over a disjoint file set (`.beads/config.yaml`, one handoff, `src/colony-page.*`, `src/server.ts`, `test/world.test.ts`); no overlap with `src/cli.ts`, `src/ambient.ts`, or `test/ambient.test.ts`. I could not run a `merge-tree` dry run (it writes objects; my profile refuses), so this is file-level disjointness rather than a proven clean merge.
- The reflog for `bead/fci.4`, and the one-line diff between `eeb8554` and `c3b8b6c`, establishing finding 9 as fact rather than inference.
- `fortkit-fci.6` exists, is open, is owned by Justin, and is scoped to the launcher injection — the gate-1 split is real, not asserted.

Taken on faith:
- **Biome lint.** My read-only profile refused every invocation I attempted (`npx biome`, `npx --no-install biome`, `npm exec -- biome`, the binary directly), and refused `fort/scripts/verify.sh` itself, so I ran the gates individually and could not close this one. The handoff claims it passed; the added code reads as Biome-formatted and the post-verification amend added a single 76-character comment line. Lint is the only gate of the five I cannot confirm against the amended tip.
- I could not execute the CLI (`node src/cli.ts ambient …` is refused under this profile), so findings 2 and 4 are read from the source, not from observed output.

The bar was met: nothing here makes the fort worse than not merging. Findings 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 9 are worth beads; 2 and 6 should be settled before `fortkit-fci.6` and `fortkit-fci.5` build on this surface, and 9 is the one I would fix as a practice, not just as a one-off correction.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — pure, UTC-clean, gate-1 split correctly; 12 non-blocking findings, none blocking; lint unverifiable

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead fortkit-fci.3, `main..bead/fci.3` — one commit, `f48ad3d` "fortkit-fci.3: render homes tavern and ambient citizens". Round one. Every acceptance criterion is met, the verifier is green and I reproduced all five of its steps myself, and nothing in the diff makes the fort worse than not merging it. Nothing blocking.

**Model attribution.** The handoff records "GPT-5 Codex"; the launcher's own record says `gpt-5.6-terra` (`fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:330`, session.start payload). Terra is the top Forge rung and the reward-hacking flag in `fort/seats/warden.md:10` is specific to Sol, but because self-report and launcher disagree I reviewed at the higher scrutiny anyway: I checked for weakened or removed checks and found none. No test is deleted anywhere in the diff; the `test/world.test.ts` edits are one new test plus coordinate/fixture updates forced by the new layout, and the `height: 620 → height: canvas.height` change in the canvas double preserves the 1:1 coordinate scale the old test relied on rather than relaxing it.

**Gate check.** The diff touches `fort/handoffs/` only — no charter text, seat file, profile, or launcher. Following the reading I recorded on fortkit-12z (finding 5), gate 1's "fort/ files" is an appositive for the constitution, so no escalation. No auth surface, no migration, nothing public-facing.

**Threat model.** Nothing here moves the surface. The page stays localhost-only (`allowedHost`), citizen-derived text reaches the canvas through `fillText` (not markup) and the panel through `esc()`, and the only new field crossing to the browser is `ColonySession`, already exposed via `benches`. No finding below bears on threats 1–4.

**What the bead asked for, and what landed.** Sessions-override-ambient is implemented in the consumer exactly as the fci.4 finding-10 comment required (`colony.ts` carries the live session object, including sessions with no bead target; `placementFor` checks it before consulting `activity()`). The on6 finding-6 drift is genuinely closed: `AmbientPlace` is now `keyof Pick<typeof buildingLayouts, …>`, so an ambient destination that is not on the map is a compile error, and display names come from the one table. Fishing and tinkering left the walls for dedicated spots. Every roster citizen is placed exactly once, and the distinct-actor guarantee is untouched — `actorStyles` is unchanged and still asserted unique.

---

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) Citizen click boxes overlap, so clicking the second citizen in a shared building selects the first.** `occupantPosition` (`src/colony-page.ts:330-335`) spaces occupants 34px apart, while the hit test (`:526-532`) accepts `x ∈ [placement.x - 15, placement.x + 46]` — 61px wide — and `placements.find` returns the lowest roster index that matches. Concrete repro with today's roster: at lunch (12:15–12:45 UTC, a shared core the ambient function guarantees for everyone) Kethra/Emrith/Ilva are all at the Tavern at x = 52 / 86 / 120; Kethra's box is [37, 98], so clicking Emrith's glyph anywhere in 86–98 opens Kethra's panel. The name label at `x - 8` starts even further inside. With 11+ co-located citizens `index % 5` and `Math.floor(index/5) % 2` wrap and two sprites coincide exactly. The prior roster grid hit-test (170px columns, `floor((x-48)/170)`) was exact, so this is a precision regression, not merely a new imprecision. Not blocking: the panel names the seat it opened, so the user can see they hit a neighbour; the ambiguous band is ~13 of 34px; and fortkit-fci.5 reworks these positions anyway. Fix is small — offset by index-within-place and size the box to the glyph. Bead.

**2. (non-blocking) `CitizenPlacement.activity` is computed but never reaches a pixel.** "lunching", "in live session", "working on fortkit-x" are produced in `placementFor` and consumed by nothing but the new test; `drawCitizen` draws glyph and name only, and `seatPanel` shows `current bead` (null when idle). A dim sprite at the Tavern is honest, but the string the code went to the trouble of computing is test-visible only. Either surface it (the spec's DF-style panel is the natural home) or drop the field. Bead.

**3. (non-blocking) The new `stripModuleSyntax` regexes are unanchored and can over-delete silently.** `src/server.ts:54-58`: `/import[\s\S]*?from\s+["'][^"']+["'];\n?/g` matches the *substring* `import` anywhere — a comment, a string literal, an identifier like `importantThing` — and then deletes everything up to the next `from "…";`, which can be most of a file. `/^export\s+/gm` will likewise strip a line inside a template literal that happens to start with `export `. Correct for all three inlined modules today, and I confirmed the composed script parses and runs (see verification), so this is fragility rather than a defect. Cheap hardening: anchor to `^\s*import\b` / `^\s*export\b`, and assert at composition time that no `^\s*(import|export)\b` survives — the same "throw at composition time" discipline fortkit-12z added for the missing marker. Bead (the 12z pattern-hardening bead is closed, so this needs a new one).

**4. (non-blocking) The composition comment in `src/colony-page.ts:12-13` is now false for its own file.** "Keep its imports type-only: runtime imports or exports would remain in the served JS" — this module now has two runtime imports, stripped by the server. It is still true for `src/world-page.ts`, which is composed *without* `stripModuleSyntax`, and that is exactly why the wording matters: a future Forge reading this comment could conclude runtime imports are now safe on the world page, where they are not. Related: the three inlined modules share one script scope, so a private-name collision (two `hash`es) becomes a page-breaking SyntaxError caught only incidentally by the VM test. Both belong in the same corrected comment. Bead.

**5. (non-blocking) The ambient identity key is not canonicalized across surfaces.** The page calls `activity(citizen.name.toLocaleLowerCase(), …)` (`:358`); `src/cli.ts:57` passes the user's argument verbatim, so `fortkit ambient Kethra` and `fortkit ambient kethra` are two different citizens and only one matches what the map shows. Latent today — I grepped `fort/scripts`, `bin/`, `civ/` and nothing invokes `fortkit ambient` yet — but fortkit-fci.6 ("Inject ambient summary at session start via launchers") is precisely where a citizen would be told she is fishing while the map shows her dining. Export a shared `ambientIdFor(citizen)` from `ambient.ts` and use it on both sides before fci.6. Bead, blocking fci.6.

**6. (non-blocking) The spec's permanent-buildings table does not list THE RIVER or TINKER BENCH, which the map now renders.** `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:50-63` names Homes and the Tavern but treats idle pursuits as ambient life, not buildings. The Overseer authorized dedicated river/tinker-bench spots in the bead comment of 2026-08-07 23:59, so this is sanctioned work, not stealth drift — but the spec is the arbiter (order 2) and spec updates are expected output (order 3), and the Forge cannot write specs. Mayor bead to amend the table (and, while there, to note that The Keep and The Palace remain listed-but-unbuilt pending fci.1/fci.2).

**7. (non-blocking) Nothing bounds the age of a "live" session, and citizen placement now depends on that.** `activeSessions` (`src/colony.ts:43-70`) treats any `session.start` with no later `session.end` as live. A crashed launcher — fortkit-izz is an open bug about exactly that class — pins a citizen at her seat indefinitely and suppresses her ambient life, which inverts the honesty property this bead exists to establish. The mechanism predates this diff (benches and `currentBead` already ride on it), so it is inherited, not introduced. The spec's own "source gaps are amber warnings" rule suggests the treatment: after some age, render the session as stale rather than as work. Bead.

**8. (non-blocking) Single-sourcing of the layout is complete except in one place.** `render()` recomputes canvas height with bare literals — `homeStartY + Math.ceil(citizens.length / 4) * 145 + 20` (`src/colony-page.ts:493-496`) — while `colony-layout.ts` keeps `homeColumns = 4` and the 145 row stride private. Change the column count in the layout module and the canvas truncates the last row of homes, which is the drift this bead was written to eliminate. Export the stride and column count, or a `homeExtent(count)` helper. Bead.

**9. (non-blocking, cosmetic) `${citizen.name}'S HOME` renders "Kethra'S HOME", and the test now pins that spelling** (`test/world.test.ts`, the canvas-height case). Separately, the sprite label dropped pronouns: `"Kethra (she/her)"` → `"Kethra"`. That is not a standing-order-10 or spec violation — the spec puts pronouns in the click panel, and `seatPanel` still shows them (`src/colony-page.ts:66`) — but it is a visible change nobody asked for, and it is the Mayor's call whether the tighter label is wanted now that names sit inside buildings.

**10. (non-blocking) Model attribution in the handoff again names no ladder rung**, repeating fortkit-12z finding 4; all 18 `Model:` lines in `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md` disagree with each other ("GPT-5 Codex", "GPT-5.6 Codex", "GPT-5.6 Terra (Codex)"). The launcher already knows the rung and writes it into `session.start`; the handoff template should take it from there rather than from self-report. Recording it here so this diff is not later read as a Sol-rung diff.

**Merge mechanics (not a finding, but the Mayor needs it).** `main` advanced during this review: `32adeb9` (merge of bead/so2) landed `fort/scripts/emit.sh`, `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh`, `test/README.md`, `test/shell.test.ts` and a handoff. `bead/fci.3` is three commits behind. `git diff bead/fci.3...main` shows zero overlap with the files this bead touches, so the merge is textually clean — but my green run is pre-merge, and the post-merge verify (which will run this bead's 62 tests plus so2's shell tests) is the one that counts.

---

### Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified myself**, in the scratch copy at `/tmp/warden-fci.3` (deps restored with `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, 52 packages, lockfile-pinned; node v24.14.0):

- **The full authoritative verifier, all five steps, green in one pass**: `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` — Node typecheck clean, browser typecheck clean, Biome "Checked 45 files, no fixes applied", Vitest **62 passed across 8 files**, ShellCheck silent. The script is `set -euo pipefail` and ran to completion, so every step passed. The handoff's "62 tests across 8 files" matches exactly. (Unlike my 12z review, Biome was reproducible this time.)
- **What I ran is what is proposed for merge**: `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/fci.3` is clean on `bead/fci.3` at `f48ad3d`, the same commit the scratch copy carries.
- **The composed page really is one working classic script.** `test/world.test.ts` executes the served script through `node:vm` and then calls `citizenPlacements` — which reaches `activity()` from `ambient.ts` and `homeLayout`/`buildingLayouts` from `colony-layout.ts` — so the three-module inline both parses (a surviving `import`/`export` would be a SyntaxError) and functions. That test is load-bearing, not decorative.
- **The sessions-override path is real, end to end**: `colony-reader` seeds `session: null`, `citizensWithActivity` fills it from `activeSessions` (session.start with no later session.end), `page-types` carries it, `placementFor` branches on it before calling `activity()`.
- **`AmbientPlace` cannot name an unmapped place**: it is derived from `buildingLayouts` keys; I confirmed the browser typecheck passes and that the `Exclude<…, home:${string}>` cast at `:361` is the only narrowing, bounded by the layout table itself.
- **Finding 1's arithmetic**, by hand from `occupantPosition`, `homeLayout` and the hit test, against the roster order `forge.md, mayor.md, warden.md` that `colony-reader` produces.
- **Event record for the work**: `bead.claimed`, `session.start`, `work.begun`, `work.ended`, `session.end (exit 0)` all present for fortkit-fci.3 on 2026-08-07, in the Mayor's mandated shape.
- **No gated path touched**, by `git diff --stat main..bead/fci.3 -- fort/ docs/ .claude/ bin/ civ/ schema/ templates/`.

**Taken on faith:**

- That the served page renders correctly in a real browser. I verified geometry, hit regions and script execution by reading and by the VM test; I did not open the page. Nothing in this seat can.
- The handoff's account of its own failed attempts (`npm ci` restoring the toolchain, the AmbientPlace narrowing fix). Unverifiable and inconsequential.
- I did not run `git merge` to confirm the clean merge; I inferred it from disjoint file sets in `bead/fci.3...main`.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: verify.sh fully reproduced green (62 tests, 8 files); 10 non-blocking findings, chief is overlapping citizen click boxes.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verifier reproduced independently in the scratch copy; diff, event stream, covenant, and spec all read. Final record below.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Work under review:** `main..bead/fci.2`, two commits (`cede7e0` implementation, `170a61b` handoff). **Model:** the launcher's `session.start` payload for `fortkit-fci.2` records `gpt-5.6-terra` — the top rung of the Forge ladder, not the reward-hacking-flagged Sol. Scrutiny weighted accordingly, but I reproduced every verifier myself rather than relying on the handoff.

The bead's acceptance criteria are met: the capital shows THE PALACE with a bench per civ office, non-capital forts render none, and the roster is parsed by the canonical `readCitizens` with pronouns taken from the files. Nothing here makes the fort worse than not merging.

---

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking, strongest) The Regent's bench can never light, because the Regent does not announce with session events.**

Occupancy flows through `activeSessions()` in `src/colony.ts:45`, which considers only `session.start` / `session.end`, keyed on `event.seat ?? event.actor`. In this fort's real stream the three civ offices announce differently:

- Chronicler: `session.start`/`session.end`, `seat:"chronicler"` — 4 events. Bench lights correctly.
- Regent: `edict.begun`/`edict.ended`, `seat:null`, `actor:"regent"` — 14 `edict.begun`. Bench never lights, including while an edict is actively running.
- Herald: reads the digest only, never fort internals; a permanently dark bench is honest for it.

This matters because the bead cites covenant section 4 as the source of occupancy, and for the Regent the section-4 announcement *is* the edict pair — charter, "The Regent, and edicts": "An edict is never silent. It emits `edict.begun` and `edict.ended` into this fort's own event stream." `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:61` assigns the Palace the question "is the civilization layer at work?", and for the fort's most active and most privileged civ seat it will always answer no.

I am not blocking on it, for three reasons. The bead said "civ session events" and the Forge implemented exactly that. The building does not fabricate a claim — "unlit" means "no open session seen for this seat", which is under-inclusive rather than false. And the Palace is capital-only and absent from `templates/`, so the mistake travels nowhere: no settlement created by fort-init inherits it. That last point is what usually decides my blocking calls, and here it points clearly at a bead.

Recommended follow-up bead: decide whether an edict counts as occupancy, and if so how a `seat:null, actor:"regent"` event maps onto the `Regent` bench (an actor→office fallback in `activeSessions`, or a separate civ-occupancy resolver). That is a Mayor-level spec decision, not a Forge fix.

**2. (non-blocking) The lit bench and the detail panel name the occupant from different fields.** `src/colony-page.ts:263` renders `lit: ${citizen.name}` (from the seat file) while `src/colony-page.ts:653` renders `lit: ${citizen.session.actor}` (from the event). For the Chronicler those are "Oswin Oncefired" and "oswin" — the two views of the same bench disagree on the occupant's name. Cosmetic, but it is exactly the kind of small divergence that gets read as a bug later. Pick one and note why.

**3. (non-blocking) A present-but-unparsable civ roster records no source gap.** `projectColony` pushes `"seats roster present, nothing parsed"` when the fort roster parses empty (`src/colony.ts:200`) but has no equivalent for `civicSeats`. The condition is visible in-building as "civic roster present, no benches", so it is not hidden — but it does not reach the `gaps` line where a reader looks for source problems.

**4. (non-blocking) Civ seats get benches but no sprites.** `citizenPlacements` and `actorStyles` iterate `projection.citizens` only, so no dwarf ever stands in the Palace. That reads as deliberate (a civ seat is not a citizen of this fort — covenant 4.3), and the bead asked for benches, not occupants. Recording it so the asymmetry is a decision rather than an oversight.

**5. (non-blocking, pre-existing, outside this diff) `bin/civ-index` is a second, divergent parser of `civ/seats/`.** Its `occupant()` extracts pronouns independently, and it derives the office name from the *filename* (`f[:-3].capitalize()`) where `readCitizens` reads the `# Seat:` heading. This diff complied with the bead's "same canonical parser" instruction; the Python duplicate predates it. Worth a bead under standing order 10's spirit, held against nothing here.

**6. (non-blocking, pre-existing) Handoff model attribution drifts from the launcher's record.** The handoff says "Model: GPT-5 Codex"; the authoritative `session.start` payload says `gpt-5.6-terra`. That exact string appears in 20 prior handoffs, so it is house-wide drift, not a defect of this bead. The charter requires the model be recorded, and it is recorded correctly in the event stream. Not a false claim — an imprecise self-report.

### What the diff got right, recorded because it was earned

- The `Array.isArray(civicSeats)` guard in `palaceBuilding` (`src/colony-page.ts:255`) is the correct check, not `?? []`. The handoff's "Failed attempts" section says the first pass normalized `null` to `[]` and would have rendered a Palace at every non-capital fort; that regression was caught by their own verification and is now covered by a test. That is the discipline working.
- Passing `handoffs = null` for the civ roster (`src/colony-reader.ts:77`) is deliberate and right: civ handoffs live in `civ/handoffs/`, and reusing the fort's handoff map would have grafted this fort's records onto civilization seats.
- The conditional spread in `projectColony` is required by `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, and it matches the existing `summaryTarget` idiom in `beadBuilding`. Not gratuitous.
- Every interpolation in the palace panel passes through `esc()`.
- Capital detection is exactly what the charter documents ("no settlement but the capital has a `civ/` directory at all") and `templates/` carries no `civ/`, so fort-init settlements can never grow a Palace.
- The three-seat roster is read from the directory, so covenant section 5's "the fifth seat when seated" needs no code change when a fourth office is appointed.

### Threat model

Nothing in this diff bears on threats 1–4. It adds read-only rendering of files the charter already declares "readable by anyone", introduces no new write path, no network fetch, and no untrusted-input surface (threat 2 untouched). The projection JSON now carries civ seat `personality` prose that is never rendered — inert, and `civ/seats/` holds no secrets, so threat 4 is not engaged. No finding here requires the out-of-scope shell-access adversary.

### Gate check

No ESCALATE trigger. The only `fort/` path touched is `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-fci.2.md`, which the charter's Memory section designates as routine seat output and which the kernel mask leaves writable; charter, seat files, profiles and launchers are untouched. Gate 1 is not engaged.

### Verified independently

- Ran `npm ci` then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in `/tmp/warden-fci.2` (the scratch copy of the candidate tree): node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (46 files, no fixes), Vitest **73 tests / 9 files passed**, ShellCheck — all green, script exited without a failure step. This matches the handoff's claim exactly, including the test and file counts.
- Read the real event stream at `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/fort/events/`: confirmed `bead.claimed`, `session.start`, `work.begun`, `work.ended`, `session.end` all emitted for `fortkit-fci.2` per the Mayor's mandatory emit recipe; confirmed the model recorded in the `session.start` payload.
- Tallied seats and categories in that stream to establish finding 1: `seat:"chronicler"` × 4 (session events), `seat:"regent"` × 0, `edict.begun` × 14 / `edict.ended` × 5 with `seat:null`.
- Read `civ/covenant.md` sections 4 and 5 and confirmed the three seated offices and the announcement rule the bead relies on.
- Confirmed `templates/` contains no `civ/` directory.
- Confirmed the `world.test.ts` palace assertions execute the real composed browser script in a `node:vm` context and assert on canvas `fillText` calls — a genuine render test, not a stub.
- Checked geometry by hand: palace at `x=275, y=545`, width 210, sharing row 4 with WALLS at `x=30` (spans to 240) — no overlap; bottom edge 657 < `homeStartY` 715; canvas width 1100.
- Confirmed `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` in `tsconfig.json`, which justifies the conditional-spread pattern.
- Confirmed `buildingLayouts` has only two consumers (`colony-layout.ts`, `colony-page.ts`), so no third enumeration of buildings went stale.

### Taken on faith

- I did **not** execute `readCitizens` against the real `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/civ/seats/*.md`; the node probe required an approval I do not hold. I traced the three real "Held by" lines against the regexes by hand — `he/him`, `they/them`, `he/him` all resolve from the first pronoun token in the parenthetical, and herald.md's later "she/her" placeholder mention is not reached because the match is first-wins. The diff's synthetic-capital reader test exercises the same code path. Confidence high, but this is inference from reading, not from running.
- No live-server render; the browser behaviour is verified only through the VM canvas mock.
- No mutation testing of the new assertions — I am read-only by construction and did not modify source to check that the tests fail without the change.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS — Palace correct & capital-only, verifier green (73/9); Regent bench can't light from edict events (bead it).

comments.text:
I have what I need. Verifier reproduced green in the scratch tree, and I checked the projection against the live `.beads/issues.jsonl`. --- Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: REQUEST-CHANGES Round one. Model that produced the work: the event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra` (`session.start`, 2026-08-07T16:36:38-08:00) — the top Forge rung, not the Sol rung carrying the reward-hacking flag. I still checked every load-bearing claim in the handoff against the real export rather than accepting it. The Keep itself is well built: the layout entry is in the single source, the drill-down works, the signal is narrow, and the Forge did the honest thing by reporting the tagging gap instead of inventing a taxonomy. One change outside the Keep breaks four existing buildings, and no test catches it. **1. BLOCKING — the queue drill-down panel for the Gate, Job Board, Trade Depot and Dungeon now renders empty.** `src/colony-page.ts:588-597` repurposed the shared `kind: "queue"` branch of `selectedPanel` to filter `projection.petitions` instead of `projection.beads`. But `beadBuilding` (`src/colony-page.ts:200-208`) hands the *same* target kind to THE GATE, THE JOB BOARD, TRADE DEPOT and THE DUNGEON whenever their queue exceeds `detailRows` (5), and `detailTargetAt` (`src/colony-page.ts:562-569`) routes the "… +N more" row to it. After this diff, clicking that row on any of those four buildings renders `

THE JOB BOARD

0 live petition(s)

    ` — the entire queue disappears, because those beads are not petitions. This is reachable with today's real data, not a corner case: `jobBoard` is every live open/blocked bead, and the live export has 80 non-closed beads, so the Job Board always overflows. The existing regression test at `test/world.test.ts:825` clicks exactly this row and asserts only `toContain("THE GATE")` — the `

    ` still carries the name, so the suite stays green while the panel body is gone. That is a shipped feature going silently blank, which is why it blocks rather than being filed. Fix is small and local: give the Keep its own target kind (e.g. `{ kind: "petitions"; name; beads }`), leave the `queue` branch rendering `projection.beads` as it was, and add a test that clicks the Job Board or Gate summary row and asserts a bead label appears in the panel — the missing assertion is as much the finding as the code. **2. Non-blocking — the founding spec is not updated, so the record will be stale at merge.** `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:66` still reads "all rows above render as of fortkit-on6/fci.3 except The Keep (fci.1) and The Palace (fci.2), which are specified here and pending their beads." More substantively, the spec's Keep row defines the signal as "gated beads, decisions, `bd human`", and this implementation can deliver none of those three as such — it delivers gate labels (currently zero in the fort) plus a prose cue. That narrowing is drift from the arbiter document and standing order 2 says flag it in the spec rather than let the two diverge silently; standing order 3 makes the spec update expected output. It lives only in the handoff and the bead comment today. Acceptance criterion 1 is "signal definition recorded" — the Mayor should not close this bead until the spec carries the narrowed definition and the status note. Non-blocking because the note is dated and scoped, so it is stale rather than false as written. **3. Non-blocking — the face count over-reports "what's blocked on me?"** I ran the projection's own predicate over the live export: 0 live beads carry a `gate-1/2/3` label, and 12 match the prose cue (the Forge saw 11 of 64; the fort has grown to 80). So the Keep renders "12 petition(s)" today, and that set includes `fortkit-fci.1` itself — in progress on the Forge bench, not waiting on Justin — along with beads that merely *mention* a gate in passing (`fortkit-8qc`, `fortkit-fci.6`). The per-petition panel is honest, labelling each as "Overseer cue in Beads text", but the building face is an unqualified count. Justin's 00:40 comment sanctions the heuristic, so this is a finding to file, not a block: suggest the face read "12 cue(s)" until real gate labels exist, and let the Mayor/Overseer tagging decision retire the heuristic. **4. Non-blocking — the source-gap disclosure is weaker than the handoff claims.** `src/colony.ts:202-204` pushes "bd human flags unavailable from issues.jsonl" on every projection that has any beads, so it is a permanent line in the shared gaps strip for every fort, sitting beside actionable gaps like "event stream ABSENT" — a gap that can never be closed trains readers to skim the strip. And the handoff says the Keep's count is "explicitly shown as [a lower bound] by the source-gap warning"; the warning is a global strip line with no visual attachment to the Keep. Better home for it is the Keep's own panel, where the reader is actually asking the question. I confirmed the underlying fact is true: no record in the live export carries any human-flag field. **5. Non-blocking — duplicate signal strings.** `src/colony.ts:113-119` maps each matching text field to the same literal, so a bead whose description *and* notes both match lists "Overseer cue in Beads text" twice. Latent today — I checked, zero live beads match in more than one field. Dedupe when convenient. **6. Non-blocking — record precision in the handoff.** The header stamps `2026-08-08T16:40:00-08:00`; the fort's own events put `work.ended` at `2026-08-07T16:40:42-08:00`. It reads like the UTC date pasted onto the local offset, which names an instant 24 hours in the future. It also records the model as "GPT-5 Codex" where the event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra` — charter standing order "every bead and handoff records which model did the work" is better served by the ladder rung. Corrections are appended, not edited in (standing order 7). **Threat model.** Nothing in this diff bears on threats 1-4, and I checked the one place it could: bead-supplied prose reaches the DOM through the Keep panel, and every interpolation goes through `esc()` (`src/colony-page.ts:592-596`), so untrusted bead text is data, not markup — threat 2 handled. Canvas details are `fillText`, not HTML. No gate-listed area is touched: the only `fort/` file added is a handoff, which is routine seat output, not constitution. **Verified independently:** ran `npm ci` then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in the scratch copy — passed all five steps (Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome across 46 files, 71 Vitest tests in 9 files, ShellCheck), matching the handoff exactly. Queried the live `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/.beads/issues.jsonl` directly: 80 non-closed beads; 0 with gate labels; 12 matching the cue regex (listed above); 6 beads carry any labels at all, so labels do flow through the export and a gate label would be seen; no field resembling a human flag exists in any record; `design` is populated on 17 records, so that branch is live rather than dead. Traced the queue-target regression by reading `beadBuilding`, `detailTargetAt` and `selectedPanel` in the merged tree and confirming no test asserts the panel body. Checked the layout arithmetic: walls at y=545 bottom out at 657, under the 720 canvas floor, and homes at 715 clear them — no bounds problem from the move. **Taken on faith:** that `bd human list` returned null at Forge time — `bd` is not runnable from this seat, though I confirmed the load-bearing half (the export carries no such flag) myself. That the 64-bead sweep was accurate at the time; my count is 80 now and consistent in shape. Fix finding 1 and this is an approve — the rest is bead material, and findings 2 and 3 should be settled before the Mayor closes rather than held against the merge. VERDICT-LINE: REQUEST-CHANGES: Keep is sound, but reusing the shared queue panel blanks the Gate/Job Board/Depot/Dungeon drill-downs, untested.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round two. Model that produced the work: `gpt-5.6-terra` again, per `session.start` at 2026-08-07T16:48:01-08:00 (`fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:398`) — same rung as round one, no ladder movement, which is the expected shape for a Forge that succeeded after review feedback. The round-2 commit is exactly the kind of fix where a model can satisfy the reviewer's *test* without fixing the *code*, so I read the restored branch and re-derived the click path myself rather than trusting the green suite.

The round-one blocker is genuinely fixed, and the requested regression guard is real.

**1. Non-blocking (resolved round-one blocker, recorded for the trail) — the shared queue drill-down is restored.**
`src/colony-page.ts:16-20` adds a distinct `{ kind: "petitions"; name; beads }` target; the Keep's `targetAt` and `summaryTarget` (`src/colony-page.ts:292-310`) now emit that kind, and the shared `queue` branch at `src/colony-page.ts:589-595` filters `projection.beads` again. I re-traced the path: `beadBuilding` still hands `kind: "queue"` to THE GATE / THE JOB BOARD / TRADE DEPOT / THE DUNGEON on overflow (`src/colony-page.ts:201-209`), `visibleDetails` gives the "… +N more" row `index: undefined` (`src/colony-page.ts:162`) so `detailIndex` falls through to `summaryTarget` (`src/colony-page.ts:563-570`), and that target now renders bead labels. The Keep's own rows are unaffected: row 0 → petitions summary, rows 1-3 → individual bead panels, overflow row → petitions summary.

The added assertion is a true guard, not a rubber stamp. `test/world.test.ts:828` asserts `gate-4 — Gate 4` in the panel body after clicking the Gate overflow row. That fixture's projection carries no `petitions` key at all, so under the round-one code the branch would have filtered `(projection.petitions ?? [])` → empty, and the assertion would have failed. `gate-4` is also outside the petition cue regex (`gate[ -]?[123]`), so it cannot be rescued by the heuristic.

**2. Non-blocking (resolved) — the Keep's face is qualified.**
`src/colony-page.ts:283-291` now reads `N cue(s)` rather than `N petition(s)`. Against the live export today that renders "12 cue(s)": I re-ran the projection's own predicate over `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/.beads/issues.jsonl` and get 82 live beads, 12 matching, 0 carrying a gate-1/2/3 label. The per-petition panel keeps its honest per-bead sourcing. This is what the Mayor's dispatch asked for and it is the right call — the face no longer asserts "waiting on Justin" about beads that are on the Forge bench.

**3. Non-blocking, new — the restored queue branch dropped a defensive guard its two siblings still carry.**
Main had `(projection.beads ?? []).filter(...)`; the restoration writes `projection.beads.filter(...)` (`src/colony-page.ts:590`). Twenty lines away, `selectedPanel`'s bead branch (`src/colony-page.ts:581-585`) and `buildings` (`src/colony-page.ts:252-256`) both still fall back to `[...unassigned, ...dungeon, ...workshops]` when `beads` is absent, and `depot` keeps `?? []` at line 265. Unreachable in production — the page fetches `/colony`, which the same server build produces in-process via `projectColony`, so the field is always present — so this is an inconsistency a future reader will trip over, not a live bug. It does bite anyone constructing a partial projection in a test, which the suite does at `test/world.test.ts:531`. Worth a bead to settle one convention across the three sites.

**4. Non-blocking, new — the restored panel does not render *exactly* as before.**
The Mayor's dispatch said restore the `queue` branch "exactly as before"; the count line changed from `N live item(s)` to `N bead(s)` (`src/colony-page.ts:593`). Cosmetic, arguably clearer, no test asserted the old string — but it is a UI-copy change to four shipped buildings, made inside a commit whose stated scope was restoration. Flagging it so the change is a decision on the record rather than a side effect.

**5. Non-blocking, carried from round one and still unaddressed — the founding spec is stale.**
`docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:60` still defines the Keep's signal as "gated beads, decisions, `bd human`" — none of which this implementation can deliver as such — and line 66 still reads "all rows above render as of fortkit-on6/fci.3 except The Keep (fci.1) and The Palace (fci.2), which are specified here and pending their beads." The Mayor's round-2 dispatch scoped the fix-up to two items and did not include this, so the Forge was right not to touch it. But acceptance criterion 1 is "signal definition recorded", and the narrowed definition lives only in a handoff and a bead comment. Standing order 2 makes the spec the arbiter and asks that drift be flagged rather than silently followed; standing order 3 makes spec updates expected output. The Mayor should land the spec edit before closing this bead, not merely before merging it.

**6. Non-blocking, carried — model attribution in the handoff.**
`fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-fci.1-round2.md:3` records "Model: GPT-5 Codex" where the event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra`. The charter's "every bead and handoff records which model did the work" is better served by the ladder rung, since failover reads the rung. The round-one timestamp defect *is* fixed: this handoff stamps 2026-08-07T16:49:32-08:00, consistent with `work.ended` at 16:49:58-08:00. The mis-stamped round-one handoff remains in the branch, which is correct — records are append-only (standing order 7).

**Merge mechanics.** The branch is behind main (main gained the `fortkit-ajj` merge since the base), so a two-dot `main..bead/fci.1` diff misleadingly shows `bin/fort-init`, `templates/fort/scripts/verify.sh`, `test/shell.test.ts` and two handoffs being reverted. I reviewed the three-dot diff. The main-ahead file set and the branch-changed file set do not intersect, so the merge should be clean without a rebase.

**Threat model.** Nothing here bears on threats 1-4. I re-checked the one surface that could: bead-supplied prose still reaches the DOM only through `esc()` in both the restored queue branch and the petitions branch (`src/colony-page.ts:593-606`), including the new `signals` join and the age string, so untrusted bead text remains data rather than markup — threat 2 handled. No gate-listed area is touched: the only `fort/` file added is a handoff, which is routine seat output, not constitution.

**Verified independently:** `npm ci` then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` in the scratch copy at /tmp/warden-fci.1 — green through all five steps (Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome across 46 files, 71 Vitest tests in 9 files, ShellCheck), run twice; I also ran the ShellCheck invocation directly since `--no-emit` suppresses the failure message, and it was silent. Read the full round-2 commit (5b8b3a6) and the branch-only three-dot source diff. Re-traced `beadBuilding` → `visibleDetails` → `detailIndex` → `detailTargetAt` → `selectedPanel` to confirm the four shared-queue buildings reach the bead-rendering branch and the Keep reaches its own. Confirmed the new assertion would fail against the round-one code. Queried the live `.beads/issues.jsonl`: 82 non-closed beads, 12 matching the cue regex, 0 carrying a gate-1/2/3 label. Confirmed `createdAt` is mapped from `created_at` in `src/readers/beads.ts:152`, so `petitionAge` works against real export data rather than only the fixture. Checked the event stream for both Forge sessions and the emit recipe compliance (`work.begun`/`work.ended` both carry `-t fortkit-fci.1`). Confirmed the spec is untouched by this branch.

**Taken on faith:** that `bd human list` returns null at Forge time — `bd` is not runnable from this seat, though I confirmed the load-bearing half (no record in the export carries any human-flag field) myself in round one.

Findings 3, 4, 5 and 6 are bead material, not merge blockers; finding 5 is the one the Mayor should settle before the bead closes, since it is an acceptance criterion rather than a nicety.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: queue-panel blocker genuinely fixed with a real regression guard; face now reads cue(s); spec still stale.
