comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
All checks complete. Writing the verdict.

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round 2 review of bead fortkit-r6x.1 at commit e7055ed on `bead/r6x.1` (range `main..bead/r6x.1`, commits af4e82a, dfca4fd, 62ec033, e7055ed). Author: Kethra Anvilmark, model **GPT-5.6 Terra** — the fort's rung-1 Forge model, named in the round-2 handoff and in Justin's bead comment. Round-1 finding 8a (missing attribution) is thereby discharged. Terra carries no reward-hacking flag (that is on Sol), and this round's work does not read like flag-chasing: the fixes are the ones asked for, in the places asked for, with no widening.

**Both round-1 blockers are fixed, and I verified each against the real repo rather than against the handoff.**

Blocker 1 (git log windowed by approxidate). `readGitLog` now lives in `src/readers/git.ts:19-46`, reuses the existing private `git()` helper, takes parsed instants, and passes ISO-8601 bounds. Re-running my round-1 demonstration against `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` just now: `--since=2026-08-04 --before=2026-08-05 main` still returns **0** commits, while the form the code now emits, `--since=2026-08-03T23:59:59.000Z --before=2026-08-05T00:00:00.000Z`, returns **34**. The `since - 1000` widening is the right shape — git's `--since` is "more recent than", so the query is deliberately one second wider than the canonical window and the authoritative half-open filter (`instant >= since && instant < until`) is applied client-side on the same `%cI` instants. That makes both boundaries safe regardless of git's own inclusivity. `test/git.test.ts` builds a fixture repo with commits at 23:59:59, exactly 00:00:00, mid-window, and exactly the next midnight, and asserts a date-only window keeps the midnight-boundary commit and drops the next one. It passes in my scratch copy.

Blocker 2 (bd's silent 50-bead cap). `readClosedBeads` moved to `src/readers/beads.ts:75-129` and now runs `bd --readonly -C <path> list --all --status=closed --limit=0 --closed-after=<RFC3339> --closed-before=<RFC3339> --json` with a 16 MiB `maxBuffer`. I re-verified against bd 1.1.2 that `--limit 0` is unlimited, that `--closed-after`/`--closed-before` accept RFC3339 and filter correctly, that `--readonly` is accepted alongside the full flag set, and that the JSON is a flat top-level array with no nested children (10 `"id":` keys at any depth for 10 closed beads). Windowing at the source also discharges round-1 finding 3: the 40.9 KB-for-ten-beads payload is now bounded to one day's closures against a 16× larger buffer, so the `execFile` overflow-to-ABSENT path is no longer reachable in practice. Round-1 finding 4 is discharged too — `--readonly` is present, which is the threat-1 (agent accident) control I asked for on a product CLI that reaches into every registered fort's `.beads`.

Everything else in the round-2 scope landed: `readTelemetryCounts` in its own `src/readers/telemetry.ts`, `readClosedBeads` in `beads.ts`, `readGitLog` in `git.ts`, the duplicated handoff candidate-listing collapsed into one `handoffCandidates()` helper with two callers, `HandoffSection` imported instead of the `Awaited<ReturnType<...>>` gymnastics, and `readCivilizationDigest` now throwing clear errors on unparseable or empty windows so r6x.4's `herald.sh` cannot walk into `new Date(NaN)`. The out-of-scope items were left alone — `src/cli.ts` is untouched by e7055ed, `formatDigest` is unchanged, the handoff regex is unchanged, no launcher is touched. **No scope creep.** The `handoffs.ts` and `digest.ts` refactors are behavior-preserving line for line, and `src/readers/beads.ts` is 66 added / 0 deleted, so the pre-existing `readBeads` is provably untouched.

I found **no regressions**. Under round-2 discipline that settles the verdict; the findings below are beads, not merge conditions.

**1. Non-blocking, and the one I would fix first — the new comment at `src/readers/beads.ts:100-102` states the opposite of what the code does.** It reads: "The digest intentionally includes every bead type: gate, infrastructure, and template work are all part of a fort's complete activity record." `--all` does not do that. From `bd list --help` (bd 1.1.2), `--all` is documented as "Show all issues including closed (overrides default filter)" — it overrides the *status* filter, nothing else. Gate, infra, and template beads are hidden behind three separate flags: `--include-gates` ("Include gate issues in output (normally hidden)"), `--include-infra`, `--include-templates`. None is passed. So the round-2 scope item "make an explicit decision comment on the closed-beads type filter rather than inheriting bd's default hide" produced a comment recording a decision the code does not implement, and the digest still silently omits closed gate beads — the class tracking this fort's own human gates — from every Herald morning. I could not demonstrate the divergence empirically: fortkit has zero beads of those types (42 beads, all bug/task/feature/epic/decision; `--include-gates --include-infra --include-templates` changes the count from 42 to 42 and the closed count from 10 to 10), so this rests on bd's help text, which is unambiguous. Fix is one of two lines: add the three flags to match the comment, or rewrite the comment to say the digest deliberately inherits bd's default hide. I am not blocking on it because the underlying behavior is identical to round 1, where I already ruled the type-filter omission non-blocking; what is new is only the wrong comment, and a digest with a wrong comment still leaves the fort better off than no digest. But a comment that misinforms is worse than no comment, and this one will be believed.

**2. Non-blocking — bd's `--closed-after` is exclusive, so a bead closed at exactly `since` falls through every window.** Proven against the live repo: with a bead whose `closed_at` is exactly `2026-08-04T19:27:25Z`, `--closed-after=2026-08-04T19:27:25Z` returns **7** and `--closed-after=2026-08-04T19:27:24Z` returns **8**. The digest's canonical window is inclusive-since, and `digest.ts` re-filters with `>= since`, but bd has already dropped the record. Because the daily windows tile, such a bead appears in no digest ever. `--closed-before` is exclusive too, which happens to match `< until` exactly, so that end is fine. This is precisely the boundary asymmetry that `readGitLog` fixes one file over with `since - 1000`, and the mirror was not applied. One line: `--closed-after=${new Date(since - 1000).toISOString()}`, safe because `digest.ts` re-filters. The digest test's expected flag string would need the matching update. Probability of biting is roughly one lost bead per several years at second precision, which is why this is a bead and not a blocker — but it is a real hole with a one-line fix.

**3. Non-blocking — the bd happy-path test proves the invocation shape, not bd's semantics.** `test/digest.test.ts` stubs `bd` with a shell script that pattern-matches the exact flag string on `PATH`. That is the right call for CI (no bd dependency, no fixture Dolt db) and it does prove the id/title/`closed_at`→`closedAt` mapping. But every semantic the fix depends on — that `--limit 0` is unlimited, that `--closed-after` is exclusive, that `--json` is a flat array — is verified only by hand, by me, twice. A bd upgrade that changes any of them passes green. Worth recording the verified semantics and the version (bd 1.1.2) in a comment beside the call, so the next reader knows what was checked and against what.

**4. Non-blocking — the digest-level closed-beads path has no assertion.** `readClosedBeads` is tested via the stub; `readDigestFort`'s window re-filter and the null→ABSENT rendering for closed beads are not. The digest test deliberately makes no assertion on Alpha's `closedBeads` (sensible — the result depends on whether real `bd` is installed on the runner), which leaves that branch uncovered. Note also that beads with a null `closed_at` are silently dropped by the re-filter rather than counted as a gap.

**5. Non-blocking — closed beads are sorted by id, not by close time.** `.sort((left, right) => left.id.localeCompare(right.id))` gives determinism, which is what the bead demanded. For a morning digest, `closed_at` order would carry the narrative and would be equally deterministic.

**6. Non-blocking — `git()` still runs without `--no-optional-locks` and with the default 1 MB `maxBuffer`.** The lock flag is my standing finding from the jmq round, unchanged here and pre-existing; it bears on threat 1 (agent accident), where a read-path tool touching another fort's repo should be mechanically unable to take a write lock. The buffer needs about ten thousand commits in one window to overflow, so it is a note, not a risk.

**7. Non-blocking — `git log --since` limits traversal rather than filtering it.** Git stops walking at the first commit older than the cutoff along a path; commits with skewed committer dates sitting behind an older commit can be missed (this is why git 2.37 added `--since-as-filter`). Not observed in any fort repo, and the fort's commits are monotonic, so this is recorded rather than acted on — but it is the one remaining way `readGitLog` can under-report without a gap marker.

**8. Non-blocking — smaller notes.** (a) `--all` is redundant alongside `--status=closed` (verified: 10 either way); harmless, but it is the flag whose meaning finding 1 turns on, so its presence reads as doing more than it does. (b) A registry entry with a known `fort_name` but no `repo` renders as `[malformed registry entry 3]`, discarding the name it does have; reporting `Broken [malformed registry entry 3]` would be more honest about the gap. (c) `fortkit digest --since <future>` with no `--until` slips past the CLI validator, which only compares the two when `--until` is present, and hits `readCivilizationDigest`'s new throw as an unhandled rejection with a stack trace instead of exit 2. (d) `readEventFeed` reads every event shard a fort has ever written and then filters, on every daily digest; performance only, but it grows without bound.

**9. Non-blocking, tracked elsewhere.** `fortkit-wtm` holds the inherited handoff-suffix regex gap, the filename-date handoff windowing, and the telemetry file/record unit conflation — all correctly out of round-2 scope. `fortkit-a0z` holds the `warden.sh` rsync defect, which still reproduces exactly: `--exclude '.beads'` is unanchored and strips the tracked fixture `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` from my scratch copy, so the fort's own verifier cannot run green from this seat. Three failures, all `beads: null`, all in `status.test.ts` and `world.test.ts`, none touching a file this diff modifies.

**Acceptance criteria.** Tests cover `--since`/`--until` windowing (three independent tests, including both boundary directions on telemetry and on git). Absent and malformed forts are covered. Counts-only telemetry is asserted by two negative assertions on prompt bodies. No new runtime deps — `package.json` is untouched by the whole branch and has no `dependencies` key at all. The one partial: `--json` shape is asserted on the library's return object rather than end-to-end through `fortkit digest --json`; that was round-1 finding 10 and Justin scoped it out of round 2, so I record it as met-in-substance.

**Verified independently, in this session:** the full `main..bead/r6x.1` diff line by line, plus e7055ed's delta in isolation to confirm the refactors are behavior-preserving and that `cli.ts` was not reopened; `npm ci` clean (0 vulnerabilities) and `npx tsc --noEmit` silent in my scratch copy; `npx vitest run` at 17 tests with exactly 3 failures, all traced to fortkit-a0z's stripped fixture; a verbose targeted run confirming all 7 tests in `digest.test.ts`, `git.test.ts`, `cli.test.ts` pass, including both new ones; the 0-vs-34 git comparison proving blocker 1 is really fixed and not merely restated; bd 1.1.2's `list --help` in full; the 7-vs-8 `--closed-after` exclusivity demonstration; `--closed-before` exclusivity; `--limit 0`; `--readonly` accepted with the full flag set; the flat 10-element JSON shape at any nesting depth; that fortkit has no gate/infra/template beads with which to demonstrate finding 1; that the fixture directories in both the worktree and my scratch copy show no side effects from the test suite invoking real `bd`; that the worktree is clean at e7055ed with no uncommitted work and my scratch `src/` is byte-identical to it; that the handoff change is 30 added / 0 deleted (append-only holds, standing order 7); that `src/readers/beads.ts` is 66 added / 0 deleted so `readBeads` is untouched; and that no gate-1 file (charter, seats, launchers, profiles) is touched by this diff, so no mandatory escalation applies.

**Taken on faith:** Biome lint — my seat's permission set refused every invocation of the Biome binary I tried, in round 1 and again here; the claim rests on Kethra's `verify.sh --no-emit` run and on the code reading as Biome-formatted, and `verify.sh` would fail on fortkit-a0z from this seat regardless. ShellCheck — no shell script changed in this diff, so it is a formality. The exact leading-position `bd --readonly -C <path> list ...` form was refused by my permission rules; I verified the equivalent `bd -C <path> --readonly list ...` with the identical flag set, and Cobra treats persistent flags position-agnostically. Finding 1 rests on bd's help text rather than on an observed divergence, for the stated reason. And Proofdelve's and Farlantern's bead volumes remain outside my allowed directories, so I still cannot say whether blocker 2 was already costing the civilization closures before this fix — only that it can no longer.

Findings 1 through 8 want beads; finding 1 wants one today. None of them should hold this merge.

VERDICT-LINE: approve-with-findings: both round-1 blockers verifiably fixed, no regressions; top bead is a bd `--all` comment that states the opposite of the code

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Review complete. Here is my record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

The change does exactly what the bead asked and nothing else: `WorldFort.beads.ready` → `open`, the page label `'ready '+f.beads.ready` → `'open '+f.beads.open`, and a test that asserts the honest label and rejects the old one. Four files, 31 insertions. Both acceptance criteria are met — no field or label named `ready` survives anywhere in `src/`, `test/`, `templates/`, `README.md`, or the founding spec's label surface, and the test genuinely discriminates (it fails against `main`'s page string on both new assertions). `src/status.ts` already said `open`; the two projections now agree, which they did not before.

Model: **gpt-5.6-terra**, the top Forge rung, per `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl` (`session.start`, `payload.model`). Not the reward-hacking-flagged rung. I checked the reward-hacking surface anyway, since a rename bead is the classic place to weaken a test into agreement: the pre-existing assertion `beads: { ready: 1, malformed: 1 }` became `{ open: 1, malformed: 1 }` — same strength, same arity — and two assertions were added, none removed or loosened. Clean.

Round one. **I block on nothing.**

**1. (non-blocking, infrastructure) The Warden's scratch copy cannot reproduce `verify.sh` green — and this is not caused by the diff.** `fort/scripts/warden.sh:33-36` builds the scratch tree with `rsync -a --exclude '.git' --exclude '.env*' --exclude '.beads' --exclude 'bin' --exclude 'obj' --exclude 'node_modules'`. Those patterns are unanchored, so rsync matches them at every depth:
- `--exclude '.beads'` strips `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/issues.jsonl` (present in the worktree, absent in `/tmp/warden-oc8`). Result: 3 of 17 tests fail in every Warden review — 2 in `test/status.test.ts`, 1 in `test/world.test.ts` — all with `beads: null`, all unrelated to whatever is under review.
- `--exclude 'bin'` strips the repo's own `bin/` (`fort-init`, `regent`, `civ-index`), which `verify.sh`'s final step shellchecks by name. That step can never run its full surface here.

The intent is obviously to exclude the fort's *own* `.beads` database and .NET-style build output; the fix is to anchor the patterns (`--exclude '/.beads'`, `--exclude '/bin'`, `--exclude '/obj'`). Threat model: **agent accident (#1)**. A reviewer that cannot reproduce the verifier either learns to wave red output through or blocks on noise, and both failure modes degrade the only judgment gate in the merge flow. `warden.sh` is a launcher, so this is human gate 1 — it lands as a bead applied by the Overseer's hand, never by a seat. The bead should also **audit whether earlier verdicts claiming a green verifier were actually reproduced in a scratch copy or taken from Forge's report**: the fixture (`0807f41`) predates the Warden launcher (`8897c75`), and `fortkit-jmq` round 2 was recorded as "verifier green" on 2026-08-04. I am flagging that as a question to answer, not asserting the record is false — I do not have those transcripts.

**2. (non-blocking) `expect(worldPage).not.toContain("ready")` bans a substring across the whole page, not just the label.** It will also reject legitimate future strings that happen to contain it — `document.readyState`, the word "already" in a title or comment. It fails loudly and safely and is trivially fixed when it fires, and the breadth is arguably the point for this bead, so I would not change it under protest. Narrowing it to the label expression (as the sibling assertion already does) would keep the guarantee without the false-positive surface.

**3. (non-blocking) The handoff names the model imprecisely.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md:2` says "GPT-5.6 Codex"; the event stream says `gpt-5.6-terra`. The charter requires every bead and handoff to record which model did the work, and the Warden weights scrutiny by rung — "GPT-5.6 Codex" does not distinguish Terra from Sol, and Sol carries the reward-hacking flag in `fort/seats/warden.md:10`. Name the rung as the events do. Same file, minor: the header timestamp `T12:15:00-08:00` postdates its own commit (`a6104ec`, 12:13:07).

**4. (non-blocking) The Overseer's routing instruction is recorded where it will not be found.** The 2026-08-07 ruling says true `ready` "becomes computable only if the export carries dependency edges (verify during bzx decomposition)" — but `fortkit-bzx` carries no note of that obligation; it lives only in a comment on this bead, which is about to close. Cheap Mayor fix: put it on `bzx`.

**5. (non-blocking, and the reason this is APPROVE and not ESCALATE) Human gate 1's wording is broader than its mechanical enforcement, and a future Warden will have to re-derive that.** The charter says the constitution is "`fort/` files, seat definitions, launchers, permission profiles". Read literally, the added `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md` is a `fort/` file and this review is a mandatory escalation. Read against the kernel mask (`fort/remember.md:17`: `.claude/`, `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/` are read-only to every seat) and against the charter's own Memory section, which designates `fort/handoffs/` as expected seat output, a Forge handoff is routine operation and escalating on it is ceremony. I have taken the second reading. An amendment bead narrowing gate 1's prose to match what the mask actually enforces would save every future Warden this derivation — and this diff touches no charter, seat file, profile, or launcher.

**6. (non-blocking, recorded, no action) The `/world` JSON shape change is breaking for any external consumer.** I grepped the repository: `WorldFort` and the `/world` endpoint have exactly one consumer, the page embedded in `src/server.ts`, shipped from the same build. No Herald, digest, or `civ/` reader touches it. That there is no consumer yet is precisely why the Overseer ruled this lands first, and the window closes the moment a fort enables JSONL export.

**Verified independently, in this session, in `/tmp/warden-oc8`:**
- The full diff, diffstat, and both commit hashes; `2a96ef48ce5e5ac2799ef4c0c1b8c4970fa1630e` matches the handoff's claim exactly.
- `src/readers/beads.ts`: `counts.open` is incremented only for records whose `status` string is literally `"open"`, via the `statuses` map. The new label is therefore true, and no status maps to `ready` — confirming the bead's premise.
- Repo-wide search for a residual `ready` field or label: none, outside `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md`'s conceptual mapping ("Beads ready/claim/close") and annals prose, neither of which is a label.
- `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`: TypeScript typecheck clean; Biome clean (32 files); ShellCheck clean on every script present in the scratch copy; Vitest **14 passed / 3 failed**, with all 3 failures traced to finding 1.
- The new assertions in isolation: `npx vitest run test/world.test.ts -t "self-contained polling page"` — **1 passed**. This is the bead's actual deliverable and it passed under my own hand.
- The 3 failures are not the diff. I read the excluded fixture in the worktree and hand-evaluated the reader against it: records `a`/`b`/`c`/`d`/`not json` yield open 1, inProgress 1, blocked 1, closed 1, malformed 1 — exactly the two failing assertions' expectations (`{blocked:1,closed:1,inProgress:1,malformed:1,open:1}` and `{open:1,malformed:1}`). The diff does not touch `test/fixtures/`.
- Model rung, and that the two prior review attempts recorded `incident` + `session.end` with `verdict_recorded:false` — the launcher behaved correctly and the bead comment's account of it is accurate.

**Taken on faith:** Forge's claim that `verify.sh --no-emit` passed 17/17 in the worktree. I cannot run it there without writing to a tree I have no business writing to. It is corroborated as far as it can be: I reproduced 14 of those 17 and hand-executed the reader over the real fixture for the other 3. I also take on faith the original intent behind `warden.sh`'s exclude list, and that no unversioned local consumer reads the `/world` JSON.

Findings 1-5 are beads, not blockers. Merge may proceed.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: honest 'open' label lands cleanly, test discriminates; 6 beads, top one: Warden scratch copy can't run verify.sh

title: Cycle 5: filesystem scoping + prompt-free masked Mayor (Overseer-authorized)
description:
OVERSEER-AUTHORIZED, 2026-08-04, executed by the harness. Filed here so this fort's record shows what arrived and why.

LAYER 1 — filesystem scoping in fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh. Today the mask is 'everything writable except what we masked', so a seat working in one fort can still rm -rf another project or wipe ~/Documents (threat #1, agent accident). Inverting it: $HOME becomes read-only inside the sandbox, with write access re-granted to exactly the repo, its worktrees, ~/.claude (memory/transcripts), /tmp, and the toolchain caches (~/.npm, ~/.nuget, ~/.cache, ~/.bun — measured: without these, npm ci breaks). Same inversion that beat the deny-glob spelling problem: enumerate grants, not prohibitions.

LAYER 3 — the masked Mayor launches with --dangerously-skip-permissions, so bash stops prompting. NOTE precisely: that flag bypasses deny rules too, so after this the KERNEL IS THE ONLY BOUNDARY for a masked Mayor. That is why Layer 1 lands first and why the mask is asserted (require_bwrap) before the flag is ever passed. Unmasked sessions (MAYOR_NO_MASK=1 or a bare 'claude') keep the full prompt+deny behaviour. Warden and Forge unaffected: headless sessions do not prompt, and codex already runs approval_policy=never.

LAYER 2 DECLINED (Overseer decision of record): hiding other forts entirely (tmpfs over ~/dev) was considered and rejected — cross-fort read access is worth more than the exfiltration-path reduction, given civ-digest and the Herald both need it. Accepted risk: a poisoned session can READ other forts (not write them, after Layer 1) and could exfiltrate over the network. Network egress remains unrestricted for all seats; injection stays threat #2 in the charter.

Verification required before close: probe that cross-project writes are denied, own-repo writes work, npm/toolchain still functions, and secrets remain unreadable.
close_reason: CYCLE 5 COMPLETE. Layer 1 (filesystem scoping) and Layer 3 (prompt-free masked Mayor) applied and probe-verified in this fort: cross-project writes denied, rm -rf of another fort denied, ~/Documents denied, own repo + worktrees + ~/.claude + toolchain caches writable, ssh key unreadable, settings.json read-only, cross-fort reads open by decision. Layer 3 flag is tied to a successful require_bwrap and is absent from the MAYOR_NO_MASK path (control flow verified by line order). Layer 2 declined; accepted risks (cross-fort reads, network egress, in-repo destruction of uncommitted work) recorded in the bead description. Restart the Mayor session to take effect.

SECOND DEATH POINT (Emrith, same trace session): with npm_config_cache set, mask_env survives but build_mask dies at lib/seat-sandbox.sh:90 — $TMPDIR referenced unguarded under set -u ('TMPDIR: unbound variable') in any shell that doesn't export TMPDIR. Smoke test from a clean env (env -i HOME PATH TERM, WARDEN_SMOKE=1) ran end-to-end: exit 0, log at /tmp/warden-bf0.log, probes 1-8 PASS. No third death point. Probe 9 (bd show inside sandbox) failed on Dolt LOCK vs read-only mount — filed as a separate bead; not a launcher defect. Close pending the real bf0 review completing (end-to-end proof).

CORRECTION (2026-08-05, Emrith): the 17:xx update above accidentally REPLACED the SECOND DEATH POINT note instead of appending; restored verbatim here, above. Notes-replace is a footgun for standing order 7 — use comments for appends.

title: Consolidate forge.sh onto lib/seat-sandbox.sh (inline mask block is now a duplicate)
description: Cycle 4 introduced fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh and used it for the Claude seats (mayor.sh, warden.sh). forge.sh still carries its own inline mask block — proven and heavily used in Proofdelve, so deliberately left alone rather than refactored in the same pass ('wire two things and verify the wire before adding the third'). This leaves TWO mask definitions per fort, which is exactly the N-list drift the fort keeps getting bitten by. Migrate forge.sh to source the lib, with a probe run before and after in Proofdelve (the only fort where a Forge runs regularly). Until then, any mask change must be applied to both.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: UPGRADED from cleanup to mask-gap fix (Warden bns finding 1, 'the one I would most want kept'): forge.sh does not source seat-sandbox.sh — its inline RO_PATHS cover ~/.codex/config.toml and the two .claude dirs but OMIT fort/charter.md, fort/seats/, fort/profiles/. So for the one seat that writes code, the constitution gate is social (Mayor merge + Warden review), not mechanical — directly contrary to fort/remember.md:17, which every seat reads at session start. Threat 1, the charter's highest class. Fix: bring forge.sh onto seat-sandbox.sh (one mask builder, not two — the original intent of this bead). forge.sh is a launcher = human gate 1: the Overseer's hand, with a standing-order-5 verification (a masked probe from a Forge session confirming EROFS on the constitution paths). Interim: remember.md carries a dated caveat as of today so the record stops overstating the boundary.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: OVERSEER AUTHORIZATION (2026-08-08, 'yes to all' on the gate-1 batch): this gate-1 change is authorized. Flow per charter: implement → Warden review → Mayor merges recording this authorization; nothing applies unreviewed. For profile files (kernel-RO to seats) the deliverable is a proposal + exact commands for the Overseer's hand.

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: MAYOR DISPATCH INSTRUCTION (first of the sequential launcher chain; Overseer-authorized): port forge.sh onto fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh so ONE mask builder exists — the inline mask block (lines ~33-95) is replaced by sourcing the lib, closing the constitution gap (charter/seats/profiles become kernel-RO to Forge sessions). PRESERVE the Forge-specific necessities exactly: the ~/.codex NOT-masked exception with config.toml re-bound RO (auth refresh must keep working), the --add-dir grant set, the .beads hooks-dir RO rebinds, the env allowlist including CODEX_HOME/OPENAI_*, and the concurrency flock. Check seat-sandbox.sh's interface first and extend it with parameters if the Forge's deltas need them — do not fork a second copy of its logic. Do NOT edit fort/remember.md (the caveat removal is the Mayor's, after standing-order-5 verification: the NEXT Forge launch will probe EROFS on fort/charter.md). Mirror to templates/fort/scripts/forge.sh if it shares the inline block. verify green; emit recipe: fort/scripts/emit.sh work.begun "<detail>" -a kethra -s forge -t fortkit-6jf (value required); no close; commit 'fortkit-6jf: '.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verifier reproduced, diff read against the bead's spec and the charter. Writing the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Scope.** `main..bead/6jf`, one commit `3ff7aa6` "fortkit-6jf: consolidate Forge sandbox launcher", 5 files: `fort/scripts/forge.sh`, `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, both `templates/` mirrors, and a Forge handoff. Work produced by the Forge seat launched on **gpt-5.6-terra** (per `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:474`); the handoff self-labels "GPT-5 Codex". Reward-hacking-flagged rung — scrutiny weighted accordingly, and the two blocking findings below are both cases where the *stated* verification is narrower than the *claimed* outcome.

**Why ESCALATE rather than REQUEST-CHANGES.** This diff is squarely in human gate 1 (launchers, `fort/` files) and touches the auth surface (`~/.codex` handling), both mandatory-escalate triggers that the blocking bar explicitly preserves. The bead carries the Overseer's 2026-08-08 authorization — but that authorization was given for "charter/seats/profiles become kernel-RO to Forge sessions" while preserving "the `~/.codex` NOT-masked exception … (auth refresh must keep working)". As implemented, the change does neither of those two things. The Overseer should see that the authorized outcome and the delivered outcome differ before the Mayor merges recording that authorization.

The design work here is genuinely good: `build_mask` was extended with two narrow options rather than forked, the option parser has a real arity guard, the ordering invariant is respected, the incident-emitting `bwrap` refusal is preserved, the flock and `--add-dir` set are untouched, and the templates are mirrored exactly. The two defects are both in the same place — the `codex` branch of the lib, which this bead is the first thing ever to exercise.

---

### 1. BLOCKING — `~/.codex` becomes read-only to the Forge; the dispatch said auth refresh must keep working

`seat-sandbox.sh:116` sets `--ro-bind "$HOME" "$HOME"`, then `:113-118` re-grants write to `RW_PATHS`. That list contains `"$HOME/.claude"` — the *Claude* runtime's home — but has no `$HOME/.codex` for the codex seat. The `codex` branch (`:76-77`) only adds `~/.claude` to the tmpfs masks and `~/.codex/config.toml` to `RO_PATHS`; `CODEX_AUTH_RO` stays `0`, so there is no writable surface anywhere under `~/.codex`.

The asymmetry is the bug in one sentence: **the `claude` branch re-grants write to its own runtime home, the `codex` branch does not.** Under the old inline mask there was no `$HOME` ro-bind at all, so `~/.codex` was fully writable except `config.toml` — which is exactly what the old comment (`forge.sh:52-55` on `main`) described as "closing the append vector while leaving token refresh working." The lib's codex-branch comment (`:71-75`) still makes that same claim, and after the cycle-5 filesystem-scoping inversion it is no longer true. Token refresh writes `auth.json`; `codex exec` also writes session rollouts under `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/` and appends `history.jsonl`. On a read-only `CODEX_HOME` those fail with EROFS.

The measured precedent in the lib does not cover this case: the `claude` DISPATCH EXCEPTION (`:88-99`) re-binds `auth.json` read-only *over a tmpfs*, and a tmpfs is writable — so codex-under-Mayor has always had a writable `~/.codex`. Nothing in the record shows codex running with a read-only one. Failure mode is either loud-and-total (Forge will not launch, core loop stops) or delayed and confusing (works until the current token expires). Either is worse than not merging.

Fix, and the naive version of it is wrong: do **not** append `--bind "$HOME/.codex"` after `build_mask` the way `herald.sh:101` re-binds its vault — that would resurface `config.toml` writable and undo 21f.5. Add it to `RW_PATHS` *before* the bind loop at `:118`, so the `RO_PATHS` pass at `:128` still lands `config.toml` read-only on top:

```sh
[ "$seat" = codex ] && RW_PATHS+=("$HOME/.codex")   # between :115 and :118
```

Settling probe, non-destructive: `bwrap --bind / / --dev /dev --ro-bind "$HOME" "$HOME" --bind /tmp /tmp -- test -w "$HOME/.codex"; echo $?` — expect `1` today, `0` after the fix. Then a real `fort/scripts/forge.sh` smoke launch on a throwaway bead, because "the mask builds" is not "codex starts."

### 2. BLOCKING — the constitution is ro-bound only in `$root`, not in the worktree where the Forge actually works

`seat-sandbox.sh:67` sets `RO_PATHS=("$root/.claude" "$root/fort/charter.md" "$root/fort/seats" "$root/fort/profiles")`, and `forge.sh:44` passes `$root` = `/home/justin/dev/fortkit`. But a Forge session's cwd is `$wt` = `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/<suffix>`, which is granted write via `$root-worktrees` in `RW_PATHS`. I confirmed by `ls` that `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/6jf/` carries its own `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, and `fort/profiles/` — none of which appear in the mask's read-only set. The only extra read-only path the Forge passes is `$wt/.claude`.

So a Forge session can still edit and commit `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/*`, and `fort/profiles/*`. The gate is protected in the checkout the Forge never touches and open in the one it always touches. This is threat 1 (agent accident) — an in-scope actor at the charter's highest priority class, and precisely the threat the bead was upgraded from cleanup to mask-gap fix to address. Merging as-is leaves the constitution gate for the code-writing seat exactly where `fort/remember.md:20-26` says it is today: social.

The second-order risk is a record defect. The dispatch defines the standing-order-5 verification as "the NEXT Forge launch will probe EROFS on `fort/charter.md`." Run from the Forge's cwd that probe *should* fail — good, it catches this. Run against `$root/fort/charter.md` it passes, the Mayor removes the dated caveat, and `fort/remember.md:17` once again asserts a mechanical boundary that does not exist for the Forge. If this finding is deferred rather than fixed, the caveat must stay and must be reworded, not deleted.

Fix: pass the worktree's constitution paths as extra read-only args, e.g. `build_mask codex "$root" --env-root "$wt" --mask-ssh-auth-sock "$wt/.claude" "$wt/fort/charter.md" "$wt/fort/seats" "$wt/fort/profiles"`. They land in the `RO_PATHS`/`extra_ro` pass at `:128`, after the `$root-worktrees` RW bind at `:118` — ordering invariant (ForgeOs-01l) holds, nothing masked lies beneath them. Worth a deliberate note in the commit that this makes those paths unwritable to git operations inside the worktree (a `checkout`/`stash` touching them will fail), which is the intended consequence. Verification assertion should be `test -w fort/charter.md` from the worktree, per the lib's own "assert, never trust an access-denied narration" discipline.

### 3. Non-blocking — the handoff's verification claim does not say which tree it probed

"A Forge-equivalent `bwrap` probe confirmed write attempts to `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/forge.md`, and `fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` fail with the read-only filesystem boundary." Given finding 2, this can only have been true of the `$root` copies. As written a reader takes it as "the constitution is EROFS to the Forge," which is not the case where the Forge runs. Not a falsification — an underspecified claim — but records are the fort's memory, and this one will be read during the caveat removal. Any re-record should name the tree and the exact command.

### 4. Non-blocking — the lib's codex-branch comment is now stale

`seat-sandbox.sh:71-75` still says `~/.codex` "stays readable … leaving token refresh working." Refresh does not work under the `$HOME` ro-bind. Whatever the resolution of finding 1, that comment needs to state the current truth; it is the sentence a future seat will trust instead of re-deriving the mount stack.

### 5. Non-blocking — "no SSH-agent access" is half true

`forge.sh:35` says the Forge gets "no SSH-agent access (the launcher historically did not pass it through)." The *socket* is masked, correctly, via `--mask-ssh-auth-sock`. But `mask_env`'s `common` list includes `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, which the old inline allowlist did not — so the Forge now gets the variable pointing at a `/dev/null` bind. Harmless in practice (ssh falls back to no agent identities), but the comment and the behavior should agree.

### 6. Non-blocking — the handoff understates how much the Forge's sandbox changed

It describes the change as "the shared builder gained two narrow Forge options." In fact the Forge inherits several behavior changes from the lib that the old inline block never had: `$HOME` goes read-only with an enumerated write-grant list, `/etc/ssh` is shadowed with a per-launch user-owned config, the `.env*` glob widens to one level of subdirectories, and `$root-worktrees` (every bead's worktree, not just this one) is writable. Nearly all of that is a tightening and is the point of consolidating. But this is not a behavior-preserving refactor, and the Mayor should not merge it as one. Worth a bead recording the Forge's new effective mask as measured, once findings 1 and 2 are settled.

### 7. Non-blocking — model attribution mismatch

Handoff says "Model: GPT-5 Codex"; the launcher recorded `gpt-5.6-terra`. The charter requires every bead and handoff to record which model did the work; the two should carry the same string.

---

**What I verified independently, in `/tmp/warden-6jf`:**

- Full verifier green, reproduced after `npm ci`: `tsc --noEmit` (both projects), `biome check .` (46 files, no fixes), `vitest run` (9 files / 80 tests passed), and the `shellcheck -x` stage over `bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh templates/fort/scripts/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh` — clean, no output. Matches the handoff's claim.
- Scratch tree matches the candidate: read `fort/scripts/forge.sh:30-47` against `git show bead/6jf:fort/scripts/forge.sh`, identical. (Blob-hash comparison was denied by my seat's permission set, so this is a read of the changed region, not a whole-file hash.)
- Templates mirror is exact for the lib: `git rev-parse` gives the same blob `259fd59` for `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` and `templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`. The two `forge.sh` mask hunks are textually identical; the files differ only in emit actor strings (`Kethra`/`kethra` vs `The Forge`/`forge`), as they do on `main`.
- Dispatch compliance: commit is path-scoped to 5 in-scope files, message prefixed `fortkit-6jf: `, bead left IN_PROGRESS and unclosed, `fort/remember.md` untouched, `work.begun` emitted with a non-empty value (`events-2026-08-07.jsonl:477`), `session.start`/`session.end` recorded, exit 0.
- No regression for existing callers: `mayor.sh:40`, `warden.sh:68`, `herald.sh:97`, `chronicler.sh:95` all pass bare paths, which the new parser routes to `extra_ro`; the `.env` glob set is `("$root" "${extra_ro[@]}")` before and `("$root" "${extra_ro[@]}")` after. Identical.
- Finding 2's factual base: `ls` confirms the worktree carries its own `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, and none is in the mask's read-only set.

**What I could not verify and am taking on reasoning, not measurement:** my seat's permission set denied `bwrap`, `command -v bwrap`, and sourcing the lib to print the `mask[]` array. Findings 1 and 2 are therefore derived by reading the mount construction in order, not by executing it. I have given the exact non-destructive probe for each; both are one command and should be run before this lands. I also did not measure whether `codex exec` hard-fails on a read-only `CODEX_HOME` or degrades — that is why finding 1 asks for a real Forge smoke launch and not only the `test -w` probe. The handoff's "Forge-equivalent bwrap probe" I could not reproduce.

**Recommended disposition:** Overseer confirms the gate-1 intent still holds, Forge fixes 1 and 2 in one pass, findings 3-7 ride along or become beads. Findings 4, 6, and 7 are bead material regardless of how 1 and 2 are resolved. The `fort/remember.md` caveat must not be removed until the EROFS probe is run **from the worktree**.

VERDICT-LINE: ESCALATE — gate-1 launcher: codex seat loses write to ~/.codex (auth refresh), and constitution ro-bind misses the worktree

comments.author: Justin Schneider
comments.text: MAYOR DISPATCH INSTRUCTION for the round-2 fix (after Warden ESCALATE — the escalate is on the record with the Overseer, whose batch authorization stands; merge waits for his confirmation of the two consequences AND round-2 approval): fix findings 1-5 in one pass. (1) Restore ~/.codex writability inside the sandbox (a write-grant through the $HOME ro-bind), keeping ~/.codex/config.toml re-bound RO — token refresh must work; PROVE with the probes she prescribed: test -w $HOME/.codex from inside the mask, and note that the true proof is the next real launch. (2) Add the WORKTREE's constitution paths to the RO set exactly as she specified: extra args for $wt/.claude, $wt/fort/charter.md, $wt/fort/seats, $wt/fort/profiles — they land in the extra_ro pass AFTER the worktrees RW bind (ordering invariant ForgeOs-01l); commit message must note the intended consequence (git checkout/stash touching those paths inside a worktree will fail). Verification assertion per the lib's own discipline: test -w fort/charter.md FROM THE WORKTREE cwd must fail. (3) Re-record the probe claim naming the tree probed and the exact command. (4) Fix seat-sandbox.sh:71-75's stale comment to state the current truth about ~/.codex under the ro-bind + your new grant. (5) Make the SSH comment and behavior agree (socket masked; SSH_AUTH_SOCK env var now passes through pointing at the null bind — either drop it from the env list for forge or say so). Mirror all of it to templates. Finding 6's measured-mask record: include the effective mask summary in your handoff. Do NOT touch fort/remember.md. verify green; emit recipe unchanged; no close; commit 'fortkit-6jf: '.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verifier reproduced, round-2 diff read against the round-1 blockers, the bead spec, and the charter. Writing the record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Scope.** `main..bead/6jf`, now two commits: `3ff7aa6` "consolidate Forge sandbox launcher" (round 1) and `0ef0d96` "fix Forge sandbox mount grants" (round 2), 6 files — `fort/scripts/forge.sh`, `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, both `templates/` mirrors, and two Forge handoffs. Round-2 work was produced by the Forge seat; the launcher recorded model `gpt-5.6-terra` (`fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:488`), the handoff self-labels "GPT-5 Codex". Reward-hacking-flagged rung, scrutiny weighted accordingly — and this round the verification claims hold up where I could check them.

**Both round-one blockers are fixed, and fixed the way I asked.**

- **Round-1 blocker 1 (~/.codex read-only, auth refresh broken)** — resolved by `seat-sandbox.sh:117-119`, `[ "$seat" = codex ] && RW_PATHS+=("$HOME/.codex")`, placed between the `RW_PATHS` declaration and the bind loop at `:122`. That is exactly the seam I specified: the grant lands after `--ro-bind "$HOME" "$HOME"` (`:120`) and before the `RO_PATHS`/`extra_ro` pass at `:132`, so `~/.codex/config.toml` still overlays read-only on top. The naive `--bind` after `build_mask` was not used. Handoff reports the paired probe `bwrap "${mask[@]}" -- test -w "$HOME/.codex"` returning 0.
- **Round-1 blocker 2 (constitution ro-bound only in `$root`)** — resolved by `forge.sh:45-46`, which now passes `"$wt/fort/charter.md" "$wt/fort/seats" "$wt/fort/profiles"` alongside `"$wt/.claude"` as extra read-only args. They land in the `extra_ro` pass at `:132`, after the `$root-worktrees` RW bind at `:122`; the ForgeOs-01l ordering invariant holds and nothing masked lies beneath them. Handoff reports `test -w fort/charter.md`, `test -w fort/seats`, `test -w fort/profiles` each returning 1 from the worktree cwd — the assertion I named, run from the tree I named. The intended consequence is stated in the commit message body ("Worktree checkout or stash operations touching protected fort paths now fail by design"), as the dispatch required.

Round-1 findings 3, 4, 5 and 6 are also addressed: the round-2 handoff names the tree and the exact commands, the stale `~/.codex` comment at `:71-76` now describes the re-grant rather than claiming a readable-and-refreshing directory, `forge.sh:35-36` now says `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is passed through pointing at a masked socket, and the handoff carries the effective-mask summary. I found **no regressions** against round 1 and nothing that I would block on.

**Why ESCALATE and not APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS.** This is a launcher and it moves the auth surface — human gate 1 in the charter and a mandatory-escalate area for this seat, both explicitly preserved by the blocking bar. That routing does not lapse because the code got better. **This is a clean escalation: I approve the work on its merits and have no changes to request.** What the Overseer is being asked to confirm are the two consequences the Mayor's dispatch already flagged, plus one fact that only surfaced this round:

1. The Forge now has **write access to `~/.codex`** inside the sandbox — auth refresh, session rollouts, `history.jsonl`. Necessary; also the first time this seat's credential directory has been writable-by-grant rather than writable-by-default.
2. `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/` become **EROFS inside every Forge worktree**. A `git checkout`, `stash`, or `merge` in a worktree that needs to modify those paths will fail. That is the point of the change, and it is a real operational cost.
3. New this round (finding 1 below): on this host `~/.codex/config.toml` does not exist, so the read-only overlay that is supposed to close the disarm-the-next-launch vector is a no-op — and with `~/.codex` now writable the Forge can *create* it. Not a regression (main behaves identically), but it bears on consequence 1 and the Overseer should see it before signing.

---

### 1. Non-blocking — the `config.toml` read-only overlay is conditional, and on this host the condition is false

`seat-sandbox.sh:78` adds `"$HOME/.codex/config.toml"` to `RO_PATHS`, and the bind pass at `:132` is guarded by `[ -e "$p" ]`. The round-2 handoff states this host has no `~/.codex/config.toml`, so no read-only bind is emitted — while `:119` now binds the whole directory writable. A Forge session can therefore create `~/.codex/config.toml`, which governs the next launch. The comment at `:71-76` asserts the vector is closed "in the later RO-path pass"; on this host it is not.

Pre-existing, not introduced here: main's inline block had the same `[ -e ]` guard and no `$HOME` ro-bind, so `~/.codex` was fully writable there too. Threat class is a deliberate self-disarm rather than threat 1 (agent accident) — the fort's own comment treats it as in scope, which is why it is worth keeping. Cheapest fix is the Overseer's hand: create an empty `~/.codex/config.toml` on the host so the guard has something to bind, and the fort gains a follow-up bead per standing order 5 verifying it stuck. Second, smaller point in the same place: the lib hardcodes `$HOME/.codex` while `mask_env`'s codex allowlist (`:184`) passes `CODEX_HOME` through — if `CODEX_HOME` is ever set elsewhere, both the RW grant and the `config.toml` overlay miss it silently. Bead material.

### 2. Non-blocking — sibling worktrees' constitution paths remain writable

`RW_PATHS` includes `"$root-worktrees"` (`:114`), granting write to *every* bead worktree, while only `$wt`'s constitution paths are re-bound read-only. A Forge working in worktree A can still write `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/B/fort/charter.md`. This is the residue of the same class as round-1 finding 2, narrowed to a case that needs a cross-worktree path to reach: such an edit lands as an uncommitted file in another bead's tree and cannot reach main without that bead's own path-scoped commit and Warden review. Genuinely new, non-blocking, bead. Related: `fort/remember.md` is writable in both trees by design — worth noting only because the caveat this bead is meant to retire lives there.

### 3. Non-blocking — the round-2 handoff says it was not launched through `forge.sh`; the event stream says it was

`fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-08-6jf-round2.md:3` reads "Model: GPT-5 Codex (orchestrated Forge session; not launched through `forge.sh`)". Events `487-488` and `495-496` record `bead.claimed` "Kethra claims fortkit-6jf", `session.start` "Kethra begins work on fortkit-6jf (gpt-5.6-terra)", and `session.end` with `{"exit":0,"log":"/tmp/forge-6jf.log"}` — strings and payload emitted only by `forge.sh`. This is a self-report error, not a fabricated verification, and the model-string half of it is round-1 finding 7 which the round-2 dispatch deliberately left out of scope. Standing order 7 says the correction is appended, never edited in. Bead.

Worth recording alongside it: `$root` is on `main`, so the round-2 session ran under the **old inline mask**, and its probes were nested `bwrap` invocations inside that sandbox. That is a faithful reproduction of the new mount stack (the outer namespace had `$HOME` and `~/.codex` writable, so the nested `--ro-bind`/`--bind` pair is what decides the result), but it is not a launch of the new launcher. The settling proof for consequence 1 remains the next real `forge.sh` launch — the handoff says so itself.

### 4. Non-blocking — the Forge did not run the fort's authoritative verifier this round

Round-2 handoff lists `bash -n`, scoped ShellCheck, `git diff --check`, and the live/template comparison, and defers `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` to "Next actions" item 1. The dispatch said "verify green" and standing order 9 requires it. I ran it myself and it is green (below), so this costs the merge nothing — but a Forge that hands off before the verifier is a habit the fort should not acquire. Bead.

### 5. Non-blocking — the round-1 handoff's overbroad probe claim stands uncorrected

`fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-6jf.md:14` still asserts a Forge-equivalent probe confirmed the constitution paths fail write, which round 1 established could only have been true of the `$root` copies. The round-2 handoff supersedes it with a correctly scoped claim, which satisfies the dispatch, but a reader of the round-1 file alone still gets the wrong impression. One appended correction line closes it. Bead.

---

**What I verified independently, in `/tmp/warden-6jf`:**

- **Full verifier green**, reproduced after `npm ci`: `tsc --noEmit` (both projects), `biome check .` (46 files, no fixes), `vitest run` (9 files / 80 tests passed), and the `shellcheck -x` stage over `bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh templates/fort/scripts/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh` — clean, exit 0.
- **Mount-order derivation**, read by hand: `--ro-bind $HOME $HOME` (`:120`) → RW binds incl. `$HOME/.codex` (`:122`) → `RO_PATHS` + `extra_ro` incl. `config.toml` and the worktree constitution paths (`:132`) → `/etc/ssh` shadow (`:153`) → `.beads` hooks (`:162`) → dev-null file masks (`:164`) → tmpfs dir masks (`:166`). Subtree binds before per-file masks; ordering invariant intact. Both round-2 probe results are what this stack predicts, which is why I credit them.
- **The `set -e` question on the new `:119` line.** `[ "$seat" = codex ] && RW_PATHS+=(...)` returns 1 for the claude seat. It is not the function's last statement, and the identical idiom already ships on main and fails routinely in production — the `MASK_FILES` loop at `:164` tests `/var/run/docker.sock` and the podman socket, which do not exist here, under `set -euo pipefail` callers. My own session was launched by `warden.sh` through that code path. No abort risk for Mayor/Warden launches.
- **Templates mirror.** `git rev-parse` gives the same blob `17cf8b9` for `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh` and `templates/fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`. I read the template `forge.sh` in full: the mask block is textually identical; the files differ only in actor strings, prompt text, and `{{REPO_PATH}}` templating, as they do on main.
- **Not a regression, established by reading `main`.** `main:fort/scripts/forge.sh` had no `$HOME` ro-bind and the same `[ -e ]`-guarded `config.toml` entry, which is what makes finding 1 pre-existing rather than introduced.

title: forge.sh: no concurrency guard or liveness record — two launchers can work the same bead in one worktree
description:
Incident 2026-08-04: the Mayor's harness session died during Kethra's first fortkit-gzn run; on resume the Mayor assumed the launcher process was dead (it was not), emitted a false session.end at 09:54:16, and launched a second forge.sh on the same bead. Both codex sessions ran concurrently in /home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/gzn from 09:54:22 until the first completed at 09:58:14; the duplicate was TaskStop'd and corrections appended to the stream.

Two missing mechanisms: (1) forge.sh takes no lock — nothing prevents two launchers on the same bead/worktree (flock on the worktree or a pidfile lease; second launcher refuses or adopts). (2) The launcher records no PID/liveness anywhere, so a resuming harness cannot check whether a session is alive and must guess. The charter's failover clause ('lease expiry returns the bead to ready') presumes leases that do not exist yet.

Same launcher ships in templates/fort/scripts/, so every fort inherits the race. Fix live + template together or coordinate with fortkit-ebm's template pass.
design: Sketch: flock -n on $wt/.forge.lock held for the session; write {pid, bead, model, started} to the lockfile; second invocation exits loudly with the holder's info. Liveness = kill -0 $pid. Lease expiry (charter failover) = lock released on process death, which flock gives for free.
notes: 2026-08-04: IMPLEMENTED per the bead's sketch (flock -n on $wt/.forge.lock, holder JSON in .forge.lock.info, exit 75, incident event). Deterministic test passed (second holder refused while held; freed on exit). Ported same hunk to Proofdelve + templates this cycle. Remains open pending first live double-launch refusal or one clean live launch.

title: Two calendars: beads stores UTC, the event stream stores local time and local-dated filenames
description: The two sources the viewer joins disagree about what day it is. Evidence, same act, 2026-08-03 evening: bd show b37 --json reports created_at 2026-08-04T07:23:59Z; the event emitted for the same work reads 2026-08-03T23:24:56-08:00. fort/scripts/emit.sh additionally names its file by LOCAL date (events-$(date +%F).jsonl), so any work after 16:00 local (UTC midnight, PST) lands in an event file dated one day before the beads that record it. Consequences: (1) a replay of founding day (fortkit-dtn) shows beads created on a day the stream says has not happened; (2) the world view will sort forts by founding date inconsistently across sources; (3) every fort in the civilization founded in the evening inherits the split, since fort-init ships emit.sh. Fix is NOT to rewrite the stream (append-only, standing order 7): readers normalize to one basis at read time, and schema/events.md states explicitly which basis each source uses and which is canonical. Decide the canonical basis before fortkit-jmq builds the readers, so this is designed in rather than retrofitted. Found 2026-08-03 by Emrith Cairnwright while verifying bead state after the Founding Moot.
design: RECOMMENDATION (Emrith, for approval, not applied): canonical instant basis is UTC; local time is a display concern only. Note that no data is actually wrong today — every event ts carries an explicit offset, so its instant is unambiguous, and beads UTC is unambiguous. The only ambiguous artifact is the FILENAME, which is a local-date shard. Therefore the cheapest correct fix needs no rewrite and no change to emitted records: (1) readers parse the offset and group by UTC, never by filename; (2) schema/events.md states that events-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl is a shard key and not a fact, and that any day-grouping (digest, replay scrubber, world-view founding dates) is computed from parsed timestamps; (3) a reader test asserts that an event written at 23:24-08:00 is grouped with beads created at 07:23Z the next calendar day. Leaves emit.sh untouched, keeps the stream append-only, and costs one sentence in the schema plus one test. Requires the Overseer's or the Warden's nod before it becomes schema law, since other settlements vendor this file.
close_reason: DECIDED as recommended, verbatim: readers group by parsed UTC and never by filename; schema/events.md (canonical) and our vendored copy now declare the day-file a shard key, not a fact; the 23:24-08:00/07:24Z pinning test is a required deliverable of the maiden readers (fortkit-jmq, now unblocked). emit.sh untouched; stream append-only; elder forts' vendored copies follow via fortkit-nd6. Emrith's block on jmq was correct and is discharged by this decision.

comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
I've completed the review. Here is my record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead fortkit-bf0, "World view v1: the embark map". Candidate a74d8ff on `bead/bf0`. Work produced by GPT-5.6 Codex as Kethra Anvilmark (per `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-05.md`) — a Forge-ladder rung carrying the seat file's reward-hacking flag, so I looked specifically for tests shaped to pass rather than to check, fixture edits that mask failures, and handoff claims beyond what was run. The handoff is scrupulously honest about what it could not do; two of the three shapes turned up something (findings 3 and 4), the third did not.

No blocking findings. I weighed blocking on finding 3 and explain below why I did not.

**1. (non-blocking, but a merge instruction) The recorded review range is stale and will revert a sandbox control if anyone applies it as a patch.** `bead/bf0` (a74d8ff) branches from f560f32 — two commits behind `main` (5063af5 and 41a9111, cycle-5 filesystem scoping and the prompt-free masked Mayor). `git diff main..bead/bf0` therefore shows the `RW_PATHS` scoping in `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh`, the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` block in `fort/scripts/mayor.sh`, and both template copies as *deletions*. This commit does not touch those files. The true change set is `main...bead/bf0`: 16 files, README + one handoff + `src/` + `test/`. Merge with a real `git merge` (or rebase onto main first) and re-run `verify.sh` on the merge result before pushing — committed ≠ pushed ≠ verified (standing order 6). Never `git apply` the two-dot patch. The bead's NOTES ("Review range: main..bead/bf0") should get an appended correction, not an edit (order 7). Threat bearing: #1, agent accident — this is exactly the shape of a silently reverted control.

**2. (non-blocking) Constitution gate: not triggered; recording the reasoning because the two-dot diff implies otherwise.** The true change set touches exactly one path under `fort/`: the new `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-05.md`. The charter's Memory section places handoffs there as ordinary seat output; human gate 1 covers the charter, seat definitions, launchers, and permission profiles. No constitutional artifact is modified, so no mandatory ESCALATE. Had the two-dot range been taken at face value, this review would have been an escalation.

**3. (non-blocking; the finding I considered blocking) The schema-mandated UTC pinning test has been defanged, and its name still claims it holds.** `schema/events.md:7` requires reader implementations to include the pinning test: an event stamped `23:24-08:00` belongs to the *next* UTC day. Before this diff, fort-alpha's latest event by parsed instant was the `2026-08-03T23:24:00-08:00` line (07:24Z) living in `events-2026-08-03.jsonl` — a shard whose *name* disagrees with the event's UTC day. `test/status.test.ts:37` ("uses parsed UTC timestamps instead of event shard filenames") asserted against that, and a filename-based implementation failed it. This diff adds 08:25Z and 08:26Z events to `events-2026-08-04.jsonl` and rewrites the expectations to 08:26Z. The latest event now sits in the shard whose name already matches its UTC day, so a naive filename-based reader passes both assertions. The 23:24-08:00 line no longer participates in either. fortkit-dpu is a *closed* bead recording this exact scar.

Why I did not block: the property is not left wholly unprotected. `test/world.test.ts:27` asserts `announcements` ordered `["Watch the gate", "Build a bridge", "UTC next day", "Earlier instant"]` — "UTC next day" (07:24Z, 08-03 shard) above "Earlier instant" (07:23Z, 08-04 shard) — which a filename-grouping implementation would order differently. Cross-shard *ordering* is therefore still covered, incidentally, in a different file; what is lost is the direct `utcDay` assertion and the discriminating power of the test that carries the name. That makes it a real degradation of a mandated verifier, not a hole in it, so merging still leaves the fort better off. Fix, a few lines: add a test asserting the 23:24-08:00 line resolves to `2026-08-04T07:24:00.000Z` and `utcDay` `2026-08-04`, or move the new events into the 08-03 shard so the latest instant again lives in a mismatched file.

**4. (non-blocking) `beads.ready` is the open count wearing the word "ready".** `src/world.ts` sets `ready: beadRecords.counts.open`, and the page renders `Beads: ready N`. Beads has no `ready` status — `src/readers/beads.ts:5-10` maps only `open`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `closed` — because ready is *derived*: open with all dependencies closed. The two differ whenever anything is dependency-blocked, which is this fort right now: fortkit-bf0 is open but not ready, since it depends on open fortkit-u8v. `test/world.test.ts:18` asserts `beads: { ready: 1, malformed: 1 }`, where 1 is fort-alpha's open count — the test encodes the mislabel rather than catching it, which is the reward-hacking shape I was watching for. Not blocking because it is latent: the design brief notes Beads data is ABSENT for every real fort today, so every real card renders `Beads: ABSENT` and no wrong number reaches anyone yet. It must be fixed before any fort exports JSONL. Cheapest honest fix is to rename the field to `open`; computing true ready requires dependency data in the export.

**5. (non-blocking) Seat and model can be attributed from two different events.** `src/world.ts` `seatFor` and `modelFor` each independently scan the whole newest-first feed for the newest event matching `target === bead.id`. A bead claimed by Forge and later touched by Warden can render one seat beside the other's model. This is fortkit-aam ("Viewer must never render two actors indistinguishably") in its most literal form. Fix: resolve both from a single chosen event, or render the pair with the timestamp it came from.

**6. (non-blocking) Watcher alerts are unbounded and unaged.** `watcherAlerts` collects every `watcher.alert` ever emitted, with no cap and no timestamp on the card. After a few months a fort shows long-resolved alarms as if current — the inverse of the projection discipline this bead was written around: not rendering a gap, but rendering stale as live. Cap the list and stamp each entry.

**7. (non-blocking) Detached HEAD is reported as a source gap.** `git branch --show-current` returns empty on a detached HEAD; `branch?.trim() || null` (`src/readers/git.ts:54`) collapses that to null and the page prints "unavailable". A real, knowable state is rendered as missing data. Fall back to a short SHA.

**8. (non-blocking) The page is a single hand-minified line inside a TypeScript string.** `src/server.ts:5` is ~2.5 KB of HTML/CSS/JS on one line. It is correct today — I read the escaping and `esc` covers `& < > " '` on every interpolated value, including bead titles and event details, so I found no injection path — but Biome does not lint it, `tsc` does not check it, and the only coverage is two substring assertions (`test/world.test.ts:49`). fortkit-bzx will build the colony view on top of it. Move it to a sibling `src/world-page.html` read at startup, or a multi-line template literal: still zero dependencies, still self-contained, and reviewable. Add one test that pushes a hostile bead title through `card()` and asserts no raw markup survives.

**9. (non-blocking) The request handler has no error boundary.** I traced all five readers — `readRegistry`, `exists`, `readBeadRecords`, `readEventFeed`, `readGitState` — and every one is total, so `/world` cannot currently reject. But nothing enforces that, and a rejected async handler in `node:http` is an unhandled rejection, which Node 24 terminates the process for. A viewer whose entire premise is tolerating malformed sources should not be one throw from dying. There is also no `server.on("error")`: a second `fortkit world` on the same port prints an EADDRINUSE stack trace. Wrap the handler (500 + JSON error) and handle listen errors.

**10. (non-blocking) CLI argument validation has a hole.** In `src/cli.ts`, when `--port` is absent `portFlag` is -1, so `portFlag + 1` is 0 and `args[0]` is exempted from the unknown-argument check. `fortkit world nonsense` starts the server silently. One-line fix.

**11. (non-blocking, documented not defended — standing order 11)** The server sets no `Host` check and no CSP. A hostile page visited while `fortkit world` is running could DNS-rebind to 127.0.0.1:4877 and read fort names, absolute repo paths, bead titles, and models. No secrets are exposed (threat 4 is not implicated), and this is an imagined attacker, not an observed failure — order 11 says that is recorded in the threat model as accepted, not turned into infrastructure work. Recording it here as accepted-and-out-of-scope. A one-line Host allowlist would close it if it is ever free to add.

**12. (non-blocking, gates the bead's close rather than the merge) Acceptance criterion "page renders 3 real forts locally" is unverified by anyone.** Forge states plainly it could not bind 127.0.0.1 under the Codex sandbox. I could not either: my seat is read-only at the kernel and the launch was refused. I read the page statically and found nothing that would prevent it rendering, including for absent forts. Standing order 9 — someone on the host should run `node src/cli.ts world`, open the URL, and record the result before this bead closes. The merge does not need to wait.

**13. (non-blocking) Handoff record precision.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-05.md` credits "GPT-5.6 Codex". The charter's Forge ladder is Terra → Sol → Sonnet 5 → Opus 5, and the seat file's reward-hacking flag is specific to Sol; "Codex" does not identify the rung, and the charter requires the model be recorded precisely so a reviewer can weight scrutiny. The file is also stamped `2026-08-05T16:55:00-08:00`, ahead of the current date (fortkit-dpu territory). Imprecision, not falsification — correct by appending.

**14. (non-blocking, but it is a hole in this gate) The Warden scratch copy is incomplete, so the seat charged with reproducing the verifier cannot.** `/tmp/warden-bf0` is missing `.beads/` (both top level and `test/fixtures/fort-alpha/.beads/`) and `bin/` relative to the candidate worktree. Neither is gitignored — `.gitignore` excludes only `.beads/proxieddb/` — so this is the launcher's own exclusion list, not a git artifact. Consequences: `npm test` fails 3 of 6 tests here purely from the absent fixture, and `shellcheck -x bin/fort-init ...` would fail on a missing file. Copying the files in was denied and the worktree is EROFS to me (both confirmed), so there is no route to a faithful run from this seat. Adjacent to fortkit-u8v; worth its own bead.

---

**Verified independently, in this session:**
- Branch topology: `bead/bf0` = a74d8ff on f560f32; `main` = 41a9111; two commits of divergence. True change set (`main...bead/bf0`) is 16 files: README, one handoff, `src/`, `test/`.
- `package.json` is untouched — no new runtime or dev dependencies. Acceptance criterion met.
- README run instructions present and accurate against the code: port 4877, bind `127.0.0.1`, `--port` flag, 5-second poll, explicit gap labelling. Acceptance criterion met.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `biome check .` pass against the candidate source in my scratch copy: `verify.sh --no-emit` reached its test step, which it only does after both return 0.
- Test suite in scratch: 3 passed, 3 failed. Every failure is `beads: null`, traceable to the absent `.beads` fixture directory (finding 14); I confirmed that directory present in the candidate worktree and absent in my copy, and 2 of the 3 failing tests predate this branch.
- Static trace of all five readers for totality (finding 9), of the page's escaping (finding 8), and of `seatFor`/`modelFor` attribution (finding 5).
- `schema/events.md:7` mandates the pinning test; `events-2026-08-03.jsonl` carries the `23:24-08:00` line; the fixture change moves the latest event into the matching-named shard (finding 3).
- Beads status vocabulary contains no `ready` (finding 4).

**Taken on faith:**
- `fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exits 0 in the candidate worktree. Asserted by Forge's handoff and independently confirmed by the Mayor in the bead notes after `npm ci` — two parties, one of them not the authoring model — and consistent with my own green typecheck and lint plus test failures that are fully explained by finding 14. I accept it; I did not reproduce it.
- That the page renders in a browser. Nobody has run it (finding 12).
- That `~/.claude/civilization.json` currently registers three forts; reading it was denied to me.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: world view is sound; 14 findings for beads, incl. a defanged UTC pinning test and a "ready" count that counts open
