comments.author: ilva
comments.text:
Verification complete. Here is my review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Subject:** `fortkit-vf2`, commit `2fbb609` on `bead/vf2` ("fortkit-vf2: canonicalize ambient citizen identity"), 6 files, +47/-5. Produced by the Forge as Kethra Anvilmark on **gpt-5.6-terra** (per `session.start` in `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:419`; the handoff records it as "GPT-5.6"). That is the top rung of the Forge ladder, not the rung carrying the reward-hacking flag (Sol), so I scrutinised the tests for tautology rather than the claims for fabrication — and found one soft test, described below, but no fabricated claim anywhere in the record.

The change itself is what the bead asked for and is made the way I would want it made: one exported function at the seam, both call sites routed through it, no other behaviour touched.

---

### 1. `ambientIdFor` canonicalizes case but not name-form, so the page and the CLI still resolve to different citizens — NON-BLOCKING (but must be beaded before fortkit-fci.6)

`src/colony-reader.ts:41` sets `citizen.name` from the seat file's `**Held by: ...**` line, i.e. the **full display name** — "Kethra Anvilmark". So `src/colony-page.ts:448` now computes `ambientIdFor("Kethra Anvilmark")` → `"kethra anvilmark"`. The fort's actor id, used in every emit recipe including this bead's own (`-a kethra`) and throughout the event stream, is `"kethra"` → the CLI computes `"kethra"`.

`activity()` derives everything — the sleep bucket (`hash(identity) % 5`), the favourite pursuit (`hash(identity) % pursuits.length`), and each meal's arrival/departure jitter — from `hash(\`${fortSeed}\u0000${citizenId}\`)`. Two different id strings are two different citizens by construction. This is the bead's own premise, applied to the spelling it did not consider: `"kethra"` and `"kethra anvilmark"` diverge exactly as `"Kethra"` and `"kethra"` did.

The bead's harm statement is therefore not yet retired: *"Latent until fci.6 injects the launcher line, where a citizen would be told she is fishing while the map shows her dining."* If fci.6 invokes `fortkit ambient kethra --since ...` — the natural invocation, and the one this very diff's `test/cli.test.ts` uses — the launcher line and the map will disagree, and the bead that was filed to prevent that will be closed.

Why this is not blocking: main has this divergence *plus* the case divergence, so merging is strictly better than not merging, and the bead's literal acceptance criteria ("one canonicalization function used by page and CLI; test proves Kethra and kethra share a schedule") are both met. The Forge built what it was told to build. The bead was underspecified, not the diff.

What I ask of the Mayor instead of a block, because this is where the fort's record gets damaged rather than its code:
- File the follow-up as a **blocker of fortkit-fci.6**, not as ordinary backlog. The resolution is a choice between two contracts — either `ambientIdFor` resolves an argument to the roster actor id (roster lookup, or first-token, deliberately chosen and written down), or fci.6 is required to pass the seat-file display name. Either is defensible; leaving it unstated when fci.6 is the consumer is not.
- When closing `fortkit-vf2`, record in the closing comment that it narrowed citizen identity to **case-folding only**. The bead's title says "canonical citizen identity across CLI, page, and launcher line"; closing it unqualified would put a claim in an append-only record that the code does not support (standing order 7).

### 2. The new `ambient.test.ts` case is near-tautological — NON-BLOCKING

`test/ambient.test.ts:18-21` asserts `ambientIdFor("Kethra") === ambientIdFor("kethra")`, then asserts the two `activity()` results are equal. The second assertion is implied by the first: both arguments come from the same function, so `ambientIdFor = () => "constant"` passes the whole test. Pinning one side to the literal — `activity(ambientIdFor("Kethra"), t, seed)` vs `activity("kethra", t, seed)` — would test the canonical *form*, not just self-consistency.

The acceptance criterion is nonetheless genuinely met, by `test/cli.test.ts:90-107`: it runs the real CLI with `ambient Kethra` and asserts the output is `Ambient schedule for kethra — 2026-08-07 UTC`. That test pins the literal lowercase form against real process output and would fail if the canonicalization were removed or changed. It is the load-bearing test here; the unit test is decoration.

### 3. The page half of the acceptance criterion is guarded by review only — NON-BLOCKING, pre-existing

`src/colony-page.ts` has no behavioural test in the suite (`test/world.test.ts:77` only asserts the script was inlined into the HTML). Nothing would catch a revert of line 448 to `citizen.name`. This gap predates the diff and fixing it is not this bead's job, but "used by page and CLI" is half-verified and the record should say so.

### 4. `toLocaleLowerCase` → `toLowerCase` on the page is a correctness improvement, and I want it noted as one — NON-BLOCKING

The page previously lowercased with the host's locale. Under `tr-TR` a browser lowers `I` to `ı` while Node's CLI would not, so page and CLI could have disagreed *for the same spelling* depending on which machine rendered the map. The handoff calls this out deliberately. It is the right call and the reasoning is sound.

Nine other `toLocaleLowerCase()` call sites remain (`src/colony.ts:118,140-141`, `src/colony-page.ts:294,297,434,477`, `src/colony-reader.ts:47`, `src/readers/handoffs.ts:86,97`), all seat-name matching against ASCII literals. I have **no observed failure** for any of them and standing order 11 forbids me filing an imagined one — I record the inconsistency as an observation, not a request.

### 5. Spec not updated — NON-BLOCKING

`docs/specs/ambient-life.md` states the contract as *"`citizenId` = actor id (`fortkit-be4`'s explicit id when it lands; display name until then)"*. This diff changes that contract (case-folded identifier) and changes user-visible CLI output (the header now echoes the canonical id, not what the user typed). The spec's "As implemented (v1.x)" paragraph is where the fort records exactly this kind of change — `fortkit-x67` earned a v1.2 note, and `d53ae50` is precedent for landing a spec update as a follow-up commit citing a Warden finding. Standing order 3 makes spec updates expected output.

I fold this into finding 1 rather than counting it separately: writing that sentence down is what would have surfaced the name-form gap in the first place. One bead, both.

### 6. Minor style — NON-BLOCKING

`src/cli.ts:58-59` calls `ambientIdFor(citizen)` in both ternary branches. A hoisted `const citizenId = ambientIdFor(citizen);` reads better and gives the canonical id a name at the seam where it matters. Trivial; take it or leave it.

### 7. Gates, records, and the emit recipe — clean, no ESCALATE

- **Human gate 1 not triggered.** The diff touches no `fort/charter.md`, no `fort/seats/`, no `fort/profiles/`, no launcher. Its only `fort/` path is `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`, which is the seat handoff mechanism and writable by design. No mandatory-escalation area is in scope.
- **Append-only honoured, and verifiably so.** The handoff discloses that the initial commit temporarily replaced this append-only file and that history was restored before amending. I checked: the diff against main is a single hunk, `@@ -668,3 +668,31 @@`, 28 insertions and 0 deletions. The restoration was exact. A self-reported near-miss on standing order 7, disclosed rather than buried, is what makes that order enforceable — it is worth saying so on the record.
- **Emit recipe followed exactly.** `work.begun` at 17:11:55 and `work.ended` at 17:14:21, both `actor=kethra seat=forge target=fortkit-vf2` (`events-2026-08-07.jsonl:420,421`).
- **No finding here bears on threats 2, 3, or 4.** Nothing in this diff touches untrusted input, dependencies, or secrets. Finding 1 sits in threat class 1 (agent accident) only in the weak sense that it would mislead a citizen about herself at session start; it is a correctness-and-honesty matter, not a security one.

---

### Verified independently

- Read the full diff and the full pre- and post-state of `src/ambient.ts`, `src/cli.ts:30-66`, `src/colony-page.ts:445-450`, both changed tests, `src/colony-reader.ts:12-55`, and `src/page-types.ts:58-67`.
- Confirmed the candidate worktree `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/vf2` is clean at `2fbb609` (== `bead/vf2` tip), and that my scratch tree's `src/` and both changed test files are byte-identical to it via `diff -r`. **My verifier ran against the candidate code, not a stale copy.**
- Ran the authoritative verifier myself in cwd after `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` (52 packages, lockfile-pinned): `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **exit 0**. Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (46 files, no fixes), Vitest **74 passed / 74, 9 files**, ShellCheck all green. This reproduces the handoff's claimed count exactly. Run twice, same result.
- Grepped every call site of `activity`, `formatAmbientDay`, `formatAmbientSince`, `ambientIdFor`, and both lowercase variants across `src/` and `test/`; confirmed line 448 of `colony-page.ts` is the only page-side `activity()` call and that no script under `fort/scripts/`, `bin/`, `templates/`, or `civ/` invokes `fortkit ambient` today.
- Confirmed the `work.begun`/`work.ended`/`session.start` events and the recorded model in the real repo's event stream.
- Confirmed the handoff hunk is a pure append against main.

### Taken on faith / not verified

- **I did not execute a schedule comparison for finding 1.** My read-only profile blocks `node -e`, so I could not print `activity("kethra", …)` beside `activity("kethra anvilmark", …)`. The finding rests on reading `hash()` and `activity()` — every per-citizen offset derives from the id string — and on the bead's own premise for the case variant. I regard it as certain in general, but I am telling you it is reasoned rather than executed, and it is cheap to confirm in one line inside a normal seat.
- I did not exercise `colony-page.ts` behaviourally; nothing in the suite does (finding 3). The page side is confirmed by reading only.
- I did not assess fortkit-fci.6's intended invocation, which does not exist yet — finding 1 assumes it will pass the actor id, which is what every other convention in this fort uses.

Merge it. The code is good sense, minimal, verified, and better than what it replaces. Do not let the bead close claiming more than it did.

I have everything I need. Verifier reproduced green in the scratch copy; scratch matches `bead/zkj` byte-for-byte.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead `fortkit-zkj`, `main..bead/zkj`, one commit `3d23884`, path-scoped, 6 files. Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** (top Forge rung, per `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:437`) — not the reward-hacking-flagged Sol, but I reproduced the verifier and traced the geometry by hand rather than accepting the handoff's arithmetic.

All six spec items land and the acceptance criteria are met: co-located citizens are individually clickable (the Tavern 52/86 repro is now a passing test), the activity string reaches the panel, the strip regexes are line-anchored with a composition-time assert, the comment is corrected and records the shared-scope collision hazard, `homeExtent()` owns the canvas extent, and the possessive is fixed and test-pinned in both places. Both fold-ins were honoured: the `ambientIdFor(" kethra")` trim case is now covered, and 1o9's payload-dedup surface was correctly left alone. The emit recipe was followed exactly, with `-t fortkit-zkj` on both `work.begun` and `work.ended`.

A bonus I verified while checking a test edit: the change also fixes a misplacement nobody named. The roster-index-6 citizen was previously drawn at (576, 931) — 34px right of and 24px above their own home's occupant slot — and now sits at (542, 955), on the bed. That is why `world.test.ts` moved its click from 576 to 546; the test update is a consequence of the fix, not a loosened pin.

Nothing here bears on the charter's threat model. The one security-adjacent surface, `stripModuleSyntax` composing source into a served page, takes input only from the repository's own files read at server start; reaching it requires already being able to edit `src/`, which is threat 1 with worse options available. The colony server remains localhost-bound via `allowedHost`. No finding.

I am not blocking. Under the ForgeOs-21f.9 bar, blocking is reserved for findings where merging makes the fort worse than not merging; not merging leaves the unclickable co-located citizens, the unanchored strip, the wrong possessive and the false comment in place. Finding 1 is nonetheless a regression this diff introduces, and I would like it fixed promptly rather than filed and forgotten.

**1. (non-blocking — regression, introduced by this diff) The walk-animation origin no longer matches where the sprite was drawn.** `colony-page.ts:542` recomputes a citizen's idle placement to use as the `from` of an idle→session walk, calling `placementFor(citizen, index, timestamp, fortSeed)` and taking the new default `indexWithinPlace = index` (`colony-page.ts:441`). But `citizenPlacements` now positions that same citizen by their index *within their place*, not their roster index. Before this diff both used `index` and agreed; now they diverge whenever `indexWithinPlace !== index`, which is the ordinary case for any citizen at roster index ≥ 1 who is not sharing a building.

Traced concretely: roster index 1, alone at the Walls at 15:00 UTC, is rendered at x = 30+22+0 = 52. On entering a session the branch at `colony-page.ts:540-548` takes `existingMotion === undefined && isInSession`, and `from.x` computes as 30+22+1×34 = 86. The sprite teleports 34px (up to 136px at index 4, or a 24px row at index 5+) and then walks smoothly to its seat building. For the live three-seat Manyhalls roster this fires on every session start for Kethra and me except during shared Tavern windows.

The root cause is the default parameter: its default value is known-wrong and its result is discarded on the first pass, so any future caller of `placementFor` silently gets the pre-fix layout. Cleanest fix is to use `previous` — it is guaranteed non-`undefined` on that branch and *is* the citizen's last rendered idle position. If the fresh-timestamp ambient position genuinely matters, the index-within-place has to be carried alongside it rather than defaulted. Either way I'd remove the default and make the parameter required.

**2. (non-blocking) `citizenPlacements` calls `placementFor` twice per citizen and throws away the first call's coordinates** (`colony-page.ts:481-487`). It is correct — `placementFor` and `activity` are pure — but it is the mechanism that forced the misleading default in finding 1. Splitting "which place does this citizen go to" (place + layout) from "where within that place" (the occupant offset) removes both the double evaluation and the wrong-by-default parameter.

**3. (non-blocking) Two spellings of the home place key.** The session branch emits `home:${citizen.name}` (raw display name, `colony-page.ts:456`); the ambient branch emits `home:${ambientIdFor(citizen.name)}` (trimmed first token, lowercased, `ambient.ts:70`). Today this is cosmetic, because `homeLayout(index)` gives every citizen their own building — but two roster names sharing a first-name token collapse to one bucket (`home:kethra`) while occupying *different* home buildings, so the second is drawn 34px off her own empty bed. This is precisely the hazard Warden c7k finding 4 flagged: the surface grew logic (`place`), identity divergence was reintroduced, and the suite stayed green. The structural fix is to key the occupancy bucket on the resolved *layout* (the building), which is what the bucket actually means, rather than on the place string.

**4. (non-blocking) The panel's `activity` is frozen at click time.** `DetailTarget` carries `activity?: string` captured on click, and `render()` re-invokes `selectedPanel(projection, selectedTarget)` on every poll (`colony-page.ts:742`). Every other field re-derives from the live projection; the one field this bead added is the one that goes stale. On the spec's "leave it on a second monitor" dashboard, a panel left open across a lunch→work transition keeps saying "lunching" while "current bead" updates beside it. `placements` is already in scope at `colony-page.ts:727`; re-deriving from the current placement rather than storing it on the target would fix it.

**5. (non-blocking) Spec drift.** `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:82` enumerates the DF-style seat panel as `name/pronouns/personality/current bead/last handoff`. `activity` was added without amending it. The bead directed the field there, so the change is right; standing orders 2 and 3 want the arbiter updated rather than silently outgrown.

**6. (non-blocking) The handoff misnames the model.** `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-zkj.md` records "Model: GPT-5 Codex"; the fort's own event stream records `gpt-5.6-terra`. The authoritative record is correct and the discrepancy is the familiar artifact of a model self-identifying, but the charter requires handoffs to record which model did the work, and my seat weights scrutiny by exactly that line. `forge.sh:6` already holds `$model` and emits it at `forge.sh:100` — a handoff should take it from the launcher rather than from the model's self-report. That is a class fix, not a correction to this diff.

**7. (non-blocking) `assertClassicScript` proves no ESM keyword survives, not that the output parses.** `^\s*export\b\s*` → `""` still silently corrupts `export default X` into `default X` and `export { x } from "./y.ts"` into a block statement, neither of which the assert catches. This is a residual hole in the "assert none survive" discipline the bead asked for, mitigated in practice because several tests `new Script(...)` the composed script and would fail on a parse error. Relatedly, `composeWorldPage` gets no assert at all; its "keep imports type-only" invariant remains comment-only, and since node's type-stripping erases `import type` to whitespace, the same assert would pass there today and could simply be applied to both.

**8. (non-blocking, nit) `homeExtent`'s `Math.max(720, …)` floor can never bind** — `homeStartY` (715) + 20 = 735 > 720 even at count 0 — and the new test `expect(homeExtent(0)).toBe(715 + 20)` pins that inertness rather than a behaviour. Faithfully carried over from the old inline expression, so not a regression. Also `homeStartY`'s `export` is now vestigial: after `colony-page.ts` dropped the import, it has no consumer outside `colony-layout.ts`.

**9. (non-blocking, nit) "world-page remains independently import-free"** (`colony-page.ts:15`) — `world-page.ts:1` does carry `import type { WorldFort }`. The accurate statement is the one world-page's own comment already makes: it keeps its imports type-only. A comment written to replace a comment that had gone false should be exact.

**10. (non-blocking) The dropped `% 2` row wrap is the right call, but leaves an undrawn boundary.** `occupantPosition` now stacks rows upward without bound, so at 11+ co-located citizens sprites climb out of the building and over the one above. The handoff discloses this and prefers it to coinciding sprites, which I agree with — distinct hit targets are the point of the bead. Worth a layout bead for a richer overflow presentation.

**Verified independently:**
- The scratch tree matches `bead/zkj` byte-for-byte — sha1 compared on `src/colony-page.ts`, `src/colony-layout.ts`, `src/server.ts`, `test/world.test.ts` against `git show`.
- `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` exits 0 in the scratch copy, all five steps: node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (46 files), Vitest 78 tests / 9 files, ShellCheck. Dev dependencies were absent and I ran `npm ci` first, matching the handoff's "Failed attempts" note; no `package.json`/lockfile change appears in the diff.
- Event stream: `work.begun` and `work.ended` both carry `-t fortkit-zkj` per the Mayor's addendum; `session.start` payload records `gpt-5.6-terra`.
- Hit-box geometry by hand: 15px box against 34px horizontal stride and 23px box height against 24px row stride give no overlap and a 1px vertical gap; the new click at (87, 470) lands in the second Tavern occupant's box [86,101] and could not have before. The `world.test.ts` click move 576→546 is a correct consequence of the index-6 home fix, not a loosened pin.
- `docs/specs/fortress-visualizer.md:82` field list, for finding 5.

**Taken on faith / not verified:**
- **Finding 1 is derived from reading the code and tracing the arithmetic, not from execution.** `node -e` is outside my read-only toolset and the probe was refused, so I could not run the two-poll transition that would demonstrate the jump. I am confident in the trace but it is unconfirmed by running code, and whoever fixes it should reproduce it first.
- Real glyph metrics. `citizenGlyphWidth = 15` / ascent 18 / descent 5 are plausible for bold 24px monospace (~0.6em advance) but I have no browser here and no test measures against actual `measureText`. The handoff's "only the 24px monospace glyph bounds receive clicks" is approximately, not exactly, true.
- That the composed page renders correctly in a real browser; I verified only that it parses and runs under `node:vm`, as the suite does.

comments.text:
All verifiers reproduced green in my scratch copy. Writing the review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Round one. Nothing here meets the blocking bar — no broken verifier, no false claim in a record, no gate that fails against the threat model, no correctness bug. The three new tests genuinely execute the shipped script and genuinely prove what they name, with one exception noted below. The category guard is correct, is mirrored into the template, and closes the `--`-as-category hole in passing. Model: **GPT-5.6 Terra** (top Forge rung; the charter's reward-hacking flag names Sol, but I weighted for the pattern anyway and looked specifically for assertions that pass without asserting — finding 1 is one, the rest are substantive).

**Gate determination (stated so it can be cheaply overruled).** The diff touches `fort/scripts/emit.sh`, and human gate 1 covers "the fort's own constitution — `fort/` files, seat definitions, launchers, permission profiles." I judge `emit.sh` outside it and therefore **not** a mandatory ESCALATE: it is a utility, not a launcher (`mayor.sh`/`forge.sh`/`warden.sh` are), not a seat definition or profile; the fort's own mechanical expression of gate 1 — the read-only set in `fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh:build_mask` — is `.claude`, `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats`, `fort/profiles`, and deliberately leaves `fort/scripts/` writable to seats. And the bead is owned by Justin and specifies this guard verbatim in its description, which is Overseer direction rather than merely Overseer permission. If he reads gate 1 as "every path under `fort/`", this is his to call, but then every handoff commit would also be gated, which the fort plainly does not practise.

---

1. **NON-BLOCKING — the "before writing" half of both negative tests is inert.** `test/shell.test.ts:41` and `:60` assert that `<root>/fort/events/events-2026-08-08.jsonl` does not exist. The failing invocations pass no `-T`, so if they *did* write, `emit.sh:50` would name the file `events-$(date +%F).jsonl`. I confirmed `date +%F` is `2026-08-07` today, and the tests pass — so on every day but 2026-08-08 that assertion is satisfied by a filename mismatch, not by the absence of a write. Consequence: if a future edit moved a guard below the write, exit code would still be 2, stderr would still match, and the ENOENT check would still pass — the regression this bead exists to catch would be invisible. The property itself *is* true of the current script (guards at `emit.sh:17-26`, first filesystem touch at `:49`; I read both copies in full). Fix is one line and strictly stronger: assert that `<root>/fort/events` does not exist at all, since `mkdir -p` runs only after the guards. Date-independent, and it also retires the timezone sensitivity in finding 6.

2. **NON-BLOCKING — the copy that actually ships to settlements is still untested and unlinted.** The bead's stated motivation is "the repo ships shell to every settlement." That shell is `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh`, and it is covered by neither the new test (which hardcodes `fort/scripts/emit.sh`) nor the verifier's ShellCheck line, which lists `bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh` and no `templates/`. The guard was mirrored by hand and nothing prevents drift. I checked both by hand this round — they are identical except the two intended placeholders (`Manyhalls`/`Proofdelve` header, `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/.git`/`{{REPO_PATH}}/.git` fallback), and `shellcheck -x` on the template is clean — but that is my eyes, not the harness. Fix: parameterize `shell.test.ts` over both copies (substituting `{{REPO_PATH}}`), and add `templates/fort/scripts/*.sh` to the ShellCheck line. This is the natural first exercise of the "grow as scripts change" clause.

3. **NON-BLOCKING — the `--` decision is sound but only half-tested.** Retaining `--` is the right call and I verified the reasoning holds: `emit.sh work.begun "" -- -a evil` → getopts stops at `--`, `OPTIND` advances past it, the residual check at `:39` sees `-a evil`, exit 2; and `emit.sh -- detail` is now rejected outright by the new category guard, which is the hole this diff closes. But the comment shipped into *both* emit.sh copies asserts "the residual-argument check below still rejects anything after it," and no test exercises anything after `--` — only a bare trailing `--` on the happy path. A shipped comment making a claim no test covers is exactly the faith-to-verified conversion this bead was filed to perform. One added case makes the comment self-verifying.

4. **NON-BLOCKING, out of scope — `civ/scripts/emit.sh` has none of the three guards.** No category guard, no detail guard, no residual-argument check (`civ/scripts/emit.sh:26-34`). It is governed by `civ/covenant.md`, not this charter, and this diff does not make it worse, so it is documented rather than blocked on. But it is the emitter the Regent and Herald use across every fort, it is the same defect class, and it bears on **threat 1 (agent accident)** — the same class as the recorded incident where the Regent's edicts went unannounced for two days (`civ/seats/regent.md:111`). Standing order 11 is satisfied: the malformed-invocation failure was observed, not imagined; it is what produced bns findings 2-4. Worth a civ-layer bead rather than a fort one.

5. **NON-BLOCKING — empty-string category still writes.** `emit.sh "" detail` is accepted and appends `"category":""`. Pre-existing and outside the bead's scope; I raise it only because it was one condition away from the guard just added, and `schema/events.md` treats categories as add-only *names*, of which the empty string is not one.

6. **NON-BLOCKING, minor — the happy-path filename is timezone-derived.** `emit.sh:50` computes the file via `date -d "2026-08-08T12:34:56Z" +%F` in **local** time. CI pins `TZ: America/Anchorage` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:16`) and the dev machine is UTC-8, so it is deterministic everywhere it currently runs; it would fail at UTC+12 or later. Not worth a change on its own — folding finding 1's stronger assertion in is the better fix.

**Acceptance criteria: all met.** emit.sh covered under `npm test` in a tmpdir with both malformed shapes and a valid write ✓; category guard added and tested ✓; harness pattern documented in `test/README.md` ✓; the finding-4 `--` question decided (retain), with the reasoning recorded in the script, the test, and the handoff ✓. The Mayor's mandatory dispatch recipe was honoured and used as the first fixture, as instructed.

---

**Verified independently, in `/tmp/warden-so2`:**
- `npm ci` (the scratch copy shipped without `node_modules`), then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → exit 0: typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (45 files), Vitest **63 tests / 9 files**, ShellCheck. Matches the handoff's claim exactly, step for step and count for count.

- `diff` of `fort/scripts/emit.sh` against `templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh` → identical but for the two intended placeholders.
- `shellcheck -x templates/fort/scripts/emit.sh` → clean (by hand; the verifier does not do this).
- `date +%F` → `2026-08-07`, which is what establishes finding 1.
- Read both `emit.sh` copies end to end: every guard precedes every filesystem touch. Read `civ/scripts/emit.sh`: no guards. Read `seat-sandbox.sh:build_mask` for the gate-1 determination, and the CI TZ pin.
- Event stream: `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:334-335` — kethra emitted `work.begun`/`work.ended` for `fortkit-so2` in the exact shape the dispatch addendum mandates.
- I could not reproduce the emit path outside a git-init'd tmpdir: my seat cannot create directories outside its working set, and running `emit.sh` from the scratch copy (which has no `.git`) would fall through to the `/home/justin/dev/fortkit/.git` default and write the **live** stream. I stopped rather than do that — which is precisely the structural blindness this bead was filed to remove, and the reason the new tests are worth having.

**Taken on faith:**
- That main stood at 60 tests and this is +3. I verified the new file contributes exactly 3 and that the suite totals 63; I did not check out main to count it, and will not mutate the real repo to do so.
- The handoff's process history — the missing pinned `vitest` and the non-fatal `packed-refs.lock` warning during commit. Not reproducible from here.
- That the author was GPT-5.6 Terra. Corroborated by the `session.start` payload `{"model":"gpt-5.6-terra"}`, which is as far as I can take it.
- That the bead comment's dispatch addendum is current Mayor law; I read it as given in the bead text.

Findings 1, 2 and 3 belong together in one follow-up bead — they are the same next increment of the harness, and finding 2 is the one I would most like to see land, because a defect in the template is the one that travels.

title: Warden sessions get nondeterministic tool permissions: full verifier some sessions, npm-only or ShellCheck-only others
description: Observed across 2026-08-07 (same launcher, same profile files): several sessions ran the FULL verifier (npm ci, verify.sh, tsc, biome, vitest, shellcheck all permitted — oc8, fyd, bzx.1/2/6, b18, kyu, sii, wkf reviews); bzx.4 round 2 was denied nearly everything (1/5 gates, ShellCheck only); fci.4 was denied biome and verify.sh; etr was denied everything EXCEPT npm ci and npm test. comments.text:
Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: ESCALATE

**Scope.** Branch `bead/hn2` = 1 commit (38485e6), 4 new files, 260 insertions: `docs/proposals/warden-allowlist/{README.md,warden-settings.diff,warden-settings.json.proposed}` and `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-hn2.md`. No product code, no `fort/profiles/` edit — the Forge correctly respected kernel-RO and the Mayor's "diagnosis + proposal, not an edit" dispatch. Work produced by **GPT-5.6** (handoff), the rung unrecorded; scrutiny weighted accordingly.

**Why ESCALATE rather than APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS.** Two reasons, both independent. (1) The verdict options make ESCALATE mandatory for the charter's gate-listed areas including the fort constitution; the entire payload of this branch is a replacement for `fort/profiles/warden-settings.json`, a permission profile — charter human gate 1 verbatim. (2) The merge itself is inert (docs + a handoff), but the artifact's purpose is a `cp -f` run by the Overseer's hand, and this review is the only gate between that file and every future Warden session — including the read-only guarantee my own seat rests on. Findings 1–3 are decisions for the person holding the `cp`, and that person is Justin. This is not a bounce back to the Forge: the diagnosis is sound and the fix is ~85% right.

**The diagnosis is correct, and I confirmed it empirically.** The launcher is deterministic (`--setting-sources ""` + one `--settings` file, `warden.sh:79-85`); nothing selects permissions per session; the variance is per-command-spelling. In *this* session, under the current unmodified profile, `npm run lint` was **denied** and `npx biome check fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` was **denied** — exactly the fci.4 symptom recorded on the bead. That is the bug, reproduced.

---

### 1. BLOCKING — the proposed file silently deletes a verified record from a constitution file

`$comment` goes from 1110 characters to 372. What is deleted, unremarked, includes:

- **"IMPORTANT, verified 2026-08-03: commands absent from the allow list are NOT reliably denied"** — the classifier auto-allows some read-only commands (sed ran; awk and python failed shut) — **"treat the allow list as convenience, the deny list as the boundary."**
- The Proofdelve 21f.8 limit: deny globs bind a *spelling*, not a file.
- The trap that deny globs match the whole command line **including quoted arguments**, so review prose containing a denied pattern trips the rule (a trap a Warden already hit once).
- The launcher contract and the Proofdelve 21f.1 provenance.

Neither the README nor the handoff mentions the replacement anywhere (`grep -niE 'comment|preserv'` returns nothing on either file). Standing order 7: records are append-only; corrections are appended, not edited in. The fort's own precedent in the same directory — `docs/proposals/izz-herald-hardening/herald-settings.json.proposed` — *preserved and extended* the caveat ("Verified caveat, same as every profile here: absent commands are not reliably denied…"). Bears on **threat 1 (agent accident)**: the deleted sentence is the one that stops a future seat from reading a longer allow list as a tighter boundary.

And the deleted finding is still true. My probes: `TZ=UTC npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` and `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` were both **permitted** with no matching rule in the current profile, while `npm run lint` was denied. The README's diagnosis paragraph opens by asserting the opposite — "Its headless default denies Bash commands not covered by that profile" — then contradicts it four bullets later. The stronger claim is the one that would survive into the applied file; the accurate one is the one being deleted.

**Fix:** append to the existing `$comment`, do not replace it.

### 2. BLOCKING — the acceptance criterion "covers the verifier's full documented invocation set" is not met, and I can demonstrate the gap

Under the proposed rules the verifier is reachable only as `fort/scripts/verify.sh…` (bare or with the enumerated env prefixes). Denied in this session, and still denied after the proposal:

- `./fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **denied**
- `/tmp/warden-hn2/fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` → **denied**

Standing order 4 says **"absolute paths always."** A Warden obeying the charter literally is denied the verifier by the profile that this bead exists to make deterministic. The README's exclusion list discloses only reversed env order, `env`, and additional variables — it never says these path spellings are out. Worse, the standing-order-5 plan prescribes only bare/relative spellings, so both verification sessions would pass green while the gap survives intact. **Fix:** add `Bash(./fort/scripts/verify.sh*)` and the absolute-path form (or, better, teach the plan to probe every spelling a charter-compliant Warden would type).

### 3. BLOCKING (risk of a broken verifier) — the collapsed formatting probably fails the fort's own lint gate

The proposal reformats `allow`/`deny` from one-rule-per-line into 9 and 3 lines of up to ~700 characters. `biome.json` includes `**` with only `node_modules`, `fort/events`, `.beads`, `.claude*` excluded, formatter **enabled**, and `npm run lint` is `biome check .` — so `fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` is in scope, and Biome's JSON formatter expands multi-element arrays past its line width. After `cp -f`, the lint gate plausibly fails for every seat, which is the "broken verifier" case at the top of the blocking bar. Corroborating: **no** in-scope JSON file in this repo has multiple array elements on one line (`grep -rEl '"[A-Za-z]+\([^)]*\)", *"' --include='*.json'` → zero hits); every profile in `fort/`, `civ/`, `templates/` and `docs/proposals/` is one-rule-per-line. The only >200-char lines in scope are `$comment` string values, which a formatter cannot break.

**I could not execute this check.** `npx biome check <path>` and `npm run lint` are both denied to me — the bug under review blocked the verification of a finding about the bug under review. So this is high-confidence reasoning from `biome.json` plus repo-wide convention, not an observed failure. It is also trivially removed: keep one rule per line. Doing so additionally fixes the artifact's reviewability — as generated, `warden-settings.diff` shows 69 allow/deny lines being deleted, and it took a `jq` set-difference to establish that the deny list is in fact byte-identical. A gate-1 artifact whose shape hides what it changes is the wrong shape.

### 4. NON-BLOCKING — 40 of the 41 added rules are of unverified necessity, and the README overstates their tightness

The README: "Reversing the two assignments, using `env`, or introducing another environment variable … remains intentionally ungranted. This keeps an allow rule tied to a known executable instead of granting `*=* *`." Both halves are unsupported. `*` in a Bash rule spans spaces — `git -C /home/justin/dev/fortkit --no-pager status --short` was permitted by `Bash(git -C * status*)` — so `Bash(TZ=* npm ci*)` matches `TZ=UTC CI=1 npm ci` and `TZ=UTC FOO=bar npm ci`; reversed order and extra variables *are* granted. Separately, `TZ=UTC cp --version` came back with the deny-rule message ("has been denied") rather than the ask message ("requires approval"), i.e. it matched `Bash(cp *)` through the env prefix, while `TZ=UTC npm ci …` and `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` were permitted with no env-prefixed rule in the file at all. The consistent reading is that the harness matches env-prefixed commands against the underlying command — in which case the `CI=1` / `TZ=*` / `CI=1 TZ=*` blocks (40 entries) are ceremony, and the README's tightness claim is wrong in the harmless direction. Nothing I can demonstrate is loosened: the deny list is unchanged and the sole allow removal (`npx vitest run*`) is subsumed by `npx vitest *`. **Recommend:** keep the explicit five-gate rules, cut the env-prefix matrix to the one documented form, and let the two-session verification settle the semantics rather than pre-paying for every combination.

### 5. NON-BLOCKING (file as a bead — highest-travel finding here) — the template profile has the identical bug

`templates/fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` — the profile `fort-init` stamps into every new settlement — carries exactly the same gaps: `npm ci`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test`, `npx vitest run`, `fort/scripts/verify.sh`, `shellcheck` and nothing for `npm run typecheck`, `typecheck:browser`, `lint`, or `npx biome`. Unlike `fort/profiles/`, the template is *not* kernel-RO to the Forge, so it was fixable in this branch. Out of the dispatched scope, so not held against the merge — but fortkit is the settlement factory, and every fort it creates today inherits the defect this bead was opened to remove.

### 6. NON-BLOCKING — minor rule hygiene

`Bash(npm run typecheck*)` already covers `npm run typecheck:browser*` (4 redundant entries once the env variants are counted). Widening `npx vitest run*` to `npx vitest *` admits `--watch` and no longer matches bare `npx vitest`. Cosmetic either way.

### 7. NON-BLOCKING — handoff records the vendor, not the rung

"Model: GPT-5.6" omits Terra vs Sol. The seat file's reward-hacking flag is rung-specific, so the rung is precisely what lets a reviewer weight scrutiny; the charter asks that every handoff record which model did the work.

### 8. NON-BLOCKING — standing order 5, satisfied in substance

No follow-up bead was filed, but the proposal carries the verification plan and hn2 stays IN_PROGRESS until both sessions land, which is the same guarantee. Noted, not charged.

### 9. NON-BLOCKING — diagnosis refinement worth appending before apply

The conclusion ("allowlist-coverage defect plus prompt variance, not launcher nondeterminism") is right. My evidence sharpens the mechanism: the dominant source of same-day variance is the **classifier deciding uncovered spellings differently across sessions**, not a hard denial from rule mismatch — `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` ran end to end for me under the *unfixed* profile. Explicit rules remain exactly the right remedy, because they remove the classifier from the five gates entirely. Worth one paragraph in the README so the next reader does not conclude the rule mismatch alone was deterministic.

---

## What I verified independently

- **Artifact consistency, by hash.** The `.diff` post-image is byte-identical to `warden-settings.json.proposed` (sha256 `2dc1f043…`), and the `.diff` pre-image is byte-identical to the live `fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` in **both** `/home/justin/dev/fortkit` and the hn2 worktree (sha256 `cc4df211…`). So the proposal is built on current reality, the two artifacts cannot disagree, and the Forge did not touch the profile.
- **Semantic delta, by `jq`.** allow 39 → 79; only removal `Bash(npx vitest run*)`, subsumed. deny 42 → 42, **zero** additions and zero removals. `defaultMode` unchanged. Top-level keys unchanged. `$comment` 1110 → 372 chars.
- **All five verifier gates, green in my scratch copy** via `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` after `npm ci` (52 packages): typecheck, typecheck:browser, `biome check .` (46 files, no fixes), vitest 9 files / 80 tests passed, shellcheck over `bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh templates/fort/scripts/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh` — exit 0.
- **Permission probes, this session, current profile.** Permitted: `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`; `TZ=UTC npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`; `TZ=UTC git -C <path> status --short`; `git -C <path> --no-pager status --short`. Denied (ask): `npm run lint`; `npm run lint 2>&1 | tail -3`; `./fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`; `/tmp/warden-hn2/fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`; `npx biome check fort/profiles/warden-settings.json`; `git -C <repo> apply --check <diff>`; `git stash list`. Denied (deny rule, distinct message): `TZ=UTC cp --version`. Compound commands are split and each part checked separately.
- **Biome scope** from `biome.json`; repo-wide absence of collapsed-array JSON; template profile gaps; `package.json` scripts.
- **Process compliance.** `bead.claimed`, `session.start`, `work.begun`, `work.ended`, `session.end` all emitted for hn2 by kethra/forge on 2026-08-07. `docs/proposals/<topic>/` layout and the `.proposed` suffix match `izz-herald-hardening` precedent.

- The handoff's claim that `git apply --check` exited 0 — that command is denied to me. Corroborated by a different route: the diff's pre-image hash matches the live file exactly, so it must apply.

- That "GPT-5.6" in the handoff names the model that did the work.

**Note for the acceptance criterion:** I reproduced all five gates this session, but only via the `CI=1` spelling and under the *pre-fix* profile, so this does **not** count as one of the two post-application confirmations.

This is now a correction appended, not edited in — exactly standing order 7, and it matches the `izz-herald-hardening` precedent.

**2. Missing verifier spellings → FIXED, and the verification plan was extended.** Added: `Bash(./fort/scripts/verify.sh*)` and `Bash(/tmp/warden-*/fort/scripts/verify.sh*)`, each also in `CI=1` and `TZ=*` forms. I re-confirmed against `warden.sh:27-28` that the scratch is `/tmp/warden-<suffix>`, so the glob is the right absolute form for a standing-order-4-compliant Warden. I re-probed all three gaps in this session under the unfixed profile: `npm run lint`, `./fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`, and `/tmp/warden-hn2/fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` were **all denied**, `npx biome --version` denied — the bug is still live and these are the rules that close it. README §Standing-order-5 now requires all six verifier spellings plus the TZ form in each of the two sessions, so a surviving gap can no longer pass green.

**3. Collapsed formatting / biome risk → DISSOLVED.** Arrays are one rule per line. The regenerated diff is 12 added lines plus 6 relocated ones against a file Biome already accepts, so there is no formatter-instability left to test: `biome check .` passed on the live file this session (46 files, no fixes), and the proposal's only formatting delta is more single-element lines in an already-expanded array plus a longer string value, neither of which the formatter rewrites. `npx biome` and `npm run lint` are still denied to me pre-fix, so I did not execute Biome against the proposed file — but unlike round one, the shape argument no longer requires it.

---

**4. NON-BLOCKING (bead) — `Bash(npx biome check*)` and `Bash(npm run lint*)` admit `--write` forms.** `biome check --write` mutates files, and `seat-sandbox.sh:92` puts `$root` and `$root-worktrees` in `RW_PATHS` for the `claude` seat type — only `.claude`, `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats`, and `fort/profiles` are re-bound read-only. So a Warden typing an absolute path could rewrite real-tree product code from a seat whose own `$comment` says it has ZERO write permissions. **Bears on threat 1 (agent accident), not on any adversary.** Severity is low and the class is pre-existing, not introduced here: `Bash(npm ci*)`, `Bash(npm install*)`, `Bash(npm run build*)` and `Bash(npx tsc*)` are already write-capable, and `git add`/`commit`/`push` stay denied so nothing escapes the working tree. Worth a bead to weigh exact-match rules (`Bash(npx biome check .)`) against reintroducing the very spelling brittleness this bead exists to remove — that trade-off is a decision, not a defect.

**5. NON-BLOCKING — `Bash(npm run typecheck*)` already subsumes `Bash(npm run typecheck:browser*)`.** One redundant entry, carried from round one. Harmless; explicitness has its own value in a file that exists to be read.

**6. NON-BLOCKING — the candidate-checkout absolute spelling is still uncovered.** `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/<x>/fort/scripts/verify.sh` has no rule. Not required — the seat prompt says reproduce verifiers *in cwd*, and cwd is the scratch — but a Warden who runs the verifier in the candidate dir lands back on the classifier. Note it in the README or accept it deliberately.

**7. NON-BLOCKING (bead) — `warden.sh:6` still carries the claim the README just retired.** Its header asserts "headless default mode auto-denies unlisted Bash commands," which is the sentence the 2026-08-03 verified record and my own probes contradict. The launcher is kernel-RO and out of this bead's scope, so it could not be fixed here — but after this lands, the profile and its own launcher will disagree in prose. A one-line gate-1 amendment.

**8. NON-BLOCKING — README prose says `/tmp/warden-<bead>/`; the launcher uses the suffix after the last hyphen** (`fortkit-bzx.4` → `/tmp/warden-bzx.4`). The glob covers both; only the sentence is loose.

**9. NON-BLOCKING — carried, being beaded by the Mayor.** `templates/fort/profiles/warden-settings.json` still has the identical gaps and stamps them into every new settlement.

---

- **Artifact fidelity, by regeneration.** `diff -u` between the live profile and `warden-settings.json.proposed`, with `a/`/`b/` labels, is **byte-identical** to the checked-in `warden-settings.diff` (empty second diff). That proves pre-image, post-image, and appliability in one shot — stronger than the `git apply --check` I cannot run.
- **Semantic delta, by `jq`.** allow 39 → 51; **zero removals**; the 12 additions are exactly the typecheck/typecheck:browser/lint/biome rules and the nine verifier path×prefix forms. deny 42 → 42, **order-identical** (`==` true). `defaultMode` unchanged. Top-level and `permissions` key sets unchanged. `$comment` prefix preserved exactly.
- **Content hashes.** Proposed file `6d2df9bc…` identical in the git blob, the hn2 worktree, and my scratch. Live profile `cc4df211…` identical across all three checkouts — the Forge did not touch `fort/profiles/`.
- **All five verifier gates green in my scratch copy.** `npm ci` (52 packages), then `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` end to end, exit 0: typecheck, typecheck:browser, `biome check .` (46 files, no fixes), vitest 9 files / 80 tests, shellcheck over `bin/fort-init bin/regent fort/scripts/*.sh fort/scripts/lib/*.sh templates/fort/scripts/*.sh civ/scripts/*.sh`. `git diff --check` clean; two-dot and three-dot diffstats agree, so main has not diverged.
- **Permission probes, this session, unfixed profile.** Permitted: `CI=1 fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`; `npm ci`; `git -C <path> …`; `jq`; `diff`; `sha256sum`. Denied: `npm run lint`; `./fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`; `/tmp/warden-hn2/fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`; `npx biome --version`; `node_modules/.bin/biome check`; `git -C <repo> apply --check`; `jq --slurpfile`. The nondeterminism is reproduced again, in both directions.
- **Process compliance.** Round two emitted `bead.claimed`, `session.start`, `work.begun`, `work.ended`, `session.end` for hn2 (kethra/forge, 18:17–18:22). Bead left IN_PROGRESS; nothing closed, merged, or pushed.
- **Record accuracy.** Every numeric claim in the round-two handoff (39→51, 12 added, 42 deny preserved exactly) checks out. Its "failed attempts" section honestly records the diff that failed `git apply --check` and was regenerated.
- Charter, `fort/remember.md`, `fort/seats/warden.md`, `warden.sh`, `verify.sh`, `seat-sandbox.sh`, `biome.json` read in full in cwd.

## What I took on faith

- The bead's session history of which commands earlier reviews were denied. I have the bead text, round one's probes, and this session's.
- That `git apply --check` exited 0 for the Forge — denied to me, but corroborated by the byte-identical regeneration above, which is a stronger guarantee.
- That Biome accepts the proposed file. Not executed (Biome is denied to me pre-fix); reasoned from `biome check .` passing on the live file plus a formatting delta the formatter does not rewrite. Round one's version of this concern is gone, not deferred.

**Note on the acceptance criterion:** I reproduced all five gates this session, but under the *pre-fix* profile and only via the `CI=1` spelling. This is **not** one of the two required post-application confirmations.

**Recommended path:** merge the docs (they change no behavior), then the Overseer runs the `cp -f` and `jq -e .` exactly as written in the README — the file is git-tracked, so the change is reversible. Then the two consecutive Warden sessions per §Standing-order-5, probing all six verifier spellings, before hn2 closes. File findings 4, 7, and 9 as beads.

comments.text:
Verifier reproduced green in my scratch copy. Writing the review record.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

Bead `fortkit-lqb`, one commit `e77c365` ("fortkit-lqb: address colony surface review findings"), 5 files, sitting directly on `main` (`7ffdc17`) — two-dot and three-dot diffs are identical, so round-1's branch-lag finding 10 does not recur. Work produced by **gpt-5.6-terra** per the launcher's `session.start` payload (the handoff and the model-authored events say "GPT-5 Codex" — see finding 6). Top rung of the Forge ladder; the seat file's reward-hacking flag on the GPT-5.6 family sent me first at the test deltas. I found no weakened assertions there: coverage is genuinely up, and the two round-1 coverage regressions (findings 2 and 3) are properly restored.

**All six acceptance criteria are met.**

- *Fixture respects declared pronouns* — `test/colony-reader.test.ts:66` now uses an invented `Dorin Stoneward` (he/him) with "in his own words". `Dorin Stoneward` and `Ari Vale` match no citizen anywhere in the repo; I grepped.
- *Row-loop restored per building* — `test/world.test.ts:488-496` loops rows 0-3 across gate/dungeon/workshop with distinct 4-bead fixtures per building, asserting row *i* opens `<prefix>-i`. Cross-building mis-wiring and the bzx.4 off-by-one class are both back under net. The overflow-row and archive and wrapped-citizen assertions are retained, not traded away.
- *Single overflow-math owner* — `detailIndex` is now `visibleDetails(building.details)[index]?.index`. I checked both branches by hand: for `len <= 5` it yields `index` when in range and `undefined` past the end; for `len > 5` it yields `undefined` on row 4, the overflow row. Identical to the old `Math.min` expression, and the no-op outer `Math.min` is gone.
- *Status visible + styled + empty-collapsed* — `#status` gets its own red-on-dark presentation (`#fff0c2` on `#5c2424`, high contrast), the `max-width: 1100px; margin: 0 auto 1rem` that `#gaps` has, and `:empty { display: none }`. `class="muted"` removed.
- *Assertions order-robust* — the two-attribute `toContain` pairs are replaced by tag-scoped regex matches on `id="ticker"` / `id="status"`, and the hardcoded `646` bounding-rect height is now `canvas.height`.
- *One stride idiom* — `workshopStride` is gone; `buildingStartX`/`buildingStride` derive all five layouts. No reference to `workshopStride` survives.

Round-1 findings 2 (truncation coverage off the render path) and 4 (duplicated overflow math) are also fixed: `building()` is called directly and `fillText` is asserted to receive `detail-0-xxx…` at y=46 and `… +3 more` at y=98, so deleting `truncateDetail` from the render path no longer leaves the suite green.

**No blocking findings.** Nothing here is a broken verifier, a threat-model gate failure, or a correctness bug. Finding 1 is the closest call and I explain below why I did not block on it.

## Findings

**1. (non-blocking) The `innerHTML` round-trip guard is defeated by apostrophes and quotes, so round-1 finding 1 is only cosmetically fixed for real data.** `src/colony-page.ts:344-346` and `:372-374` compute the markup and assign only `if (detailPanel.innerHTML !== panelMarkup)`. But reading `innerHTML` back returns the *serialized* subtree, and the HTML fragment serializer escapes only `&`, `<`, `>` and U+00A0 in text nodes — it does **not** re-escape quotes. `esc()` emits `"` and `'`; the parser turns those into `"` and `'`; the serializer returns them as `"` and `'`. So for any panel whose text contains an apostrophe or a double quote, `innerHTML !== panelMarkup` is permanently true and the `aria-live="polite"` region is rewritten on every 5-second poll exactly as before. **122 of the 127 records in `.beads/issues.jsonl` contain an apostrophe** — including this bead's own description ("standing order 10's spirit"). The guard therefore helps for the empty-panel case (which was already benign: replacing no children with no children queues no mutation record) and for quote-free content, and does nothing for essentially every real bead panel.

The handoff records this under **Verified facts** as "keeps the detail panel stable across identical polling projections". That claim is unsupported — nothing in the verifier exercises it, and no test was added — and it is false for the common case. I considered blocking under the bar's "false or unsupported claim in a record" head and landed against it, for two reasons. First, the counterfactual: the guard is *harmless* when it fails (behavior is identical to pre-merge), the six acceptance criteria are all met, and finding 1 is named in the bead's description but is not one of the criteria. Not merging leaves a misgendered fixture of a real citizen committed, the row-loop net missing before on6 rewrites this surface, duplicated overflow math, and an invisible error channel. Merging is plainly better. Second, standing order 7 says corrections are appended, not edited in — this review is that append. The fix is to compare against a stored previous-markup variable rather than reading back the DOM, and to assert it with an `innerHTML` setter spy (the test doubles are already plain objects, so a spy is two lines). File as a bead; put it at the top, because on6 inherits this surface.

**2. (non-blocking) `#status` is the other live region and it still churns.** `src/colony-page.ts:390-393` sets `status.textContent` to the same `Colony data unavailable: …` string on every failed poll. `role="status"` is an implicit `aria-live="polite"` region, and assigning identical text still replaces the text node, so a persistent outage re-announces every five seconds. This is pre-existing from `fortkit-etr`, not a regression from this diff, and round-1 finding 1 named only `#detail-panel` — but the bead framed item (1) as the "aria/status poll churn item", so I record that the status half is unaddressed. The success path (`textContent = ""` when already empty) is genuinely a no-op and needs nothing.

**3. (non-blocking) Collapsing a live region with `:empty { display: none }` may cost the announcement it was meant to carry.** `src/colony-page.html:12` puts the collapse rule on `#status` itself, which is the element carrying `role="status"`. At the moment the error text is inserted the element is still matching `:empty` and therefore `display: none`; screen-reader handling of content added to a hidden live region is inconsistent, and this is the page's only error channel. Round-1 finding 7 asked for `:empty`, so the Forge did exactly what was asked — this is a refinement, not a miss. The robust shape is to collapse a wrapper and leave the live region always rendered, or to zero the margin when empty rather than removing the box from the tree.

**4. (non-blocking) `#gaps` silently changed colour.** The old rule was `#gaps, #detail-panel { …; color: #ffba8c; }`; the new one drops `color` entirely (`src/colony-page.html:11`). `#detail-panel` is unaffected because its own rule sets `#e8ddbf` two lines down, but `#gaps` carries `class="muted"` and the ID rule was the only thing outranking it — so the source-gaps line goes from amber `#ffba8c` to grey `#b9aa8d`. That is a rendered-output change to a data-completeness warning, in the same commit that argues warnings should be *more* visible, and it appears in neither the bead nor the handoff. It may well be the intent of `class="muted"`; it should be a decision rather than a side effect.

**5. (non-blocking) A second fixture still casts a real citizen.** `test/colony-reader.test.ts:167` writes `**Held by: Kethra Anvilmark** (unparseable)` and asserts pronouns `—`. This does not *contradict* a declared pronoun the way line 66 did, so it is not the standing-order-10 problem that put finding 5 at the top of this bead; it is the same class one notch down — this fort's real Forge holder, in a committed file, rendered as having no parseable pronouns. Use an invented holder here too, for the same reason and at the same cost.

**6. (non-blocking) Two different model strings for one session.** `fort/events/events-2026-08-07.jsonl:271` (launcher-emitted) records `gpt-5.6-terra`; lines 272 and 274 and the handoff (model-authored) record `GPT-5 Codex`, which is not a rung on the charter's Forge ladder. The charter requires every bead and handoff to record which model did the work; a self-reported approximation that disagrees with the launcher's authoritative value defeats that, and it is precisely the field a reviewer uses to calibrate scrutiny. Have the seat scripts inject the launcher's model id rather than letting the model name itself.

**7. (non-blocking) Residual test nits from item 8.** `expect(colonyPage).toContain('<canvas id="colony"')` at `test/world.test.ts:87` still requires `id` to be the canvas tag's first attribute — the same brittleness class, just single-attribute. And `test/world.test.ts:170` still casts `visibleDetails` as `(values: string[]) => string[]` while it now returns `VisibleDetail[]`; the `toEqual` below would catch a real regression at runtime, but the cast is now knowingly wrong and hides the signature from the typechecker.

## Gate and threat-model position

**No human gate is engaged, and no escalation is warranted.** The commit's only `fort/` path is `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07-lqb.md`. Gate 1's subject is the fort's constitution — charter, seat definitions, launchers, permission profiles — and the kernel mask makes exactly those read-only while leaving `fort/handoffs/` writable by design. Handoffs are ordinary per-session work records. This matches the reasoning accepted at `fortkit-etr`.

**No finding bears on the charter's threat model.** Nothing here touches secrets, launchers, or privileged scripts (threats 1, 3, 4). Threat 2 — untrusted bead and seat text rendered into HTML — is the live surface, and it is unchanged: `esc()` is byte-identical, the hostile-payload assertions for `seatPanel`/`beadPanel`/`card` are intact and green, and the newly-styled `#status` writes the interpolated `${error}` via `textContent`, not `innerHTML`, so it cannot inject markup. Findings 1, 2 and 3 are accessibility; 4 is presentation; 5, 6 and 7 are records and test hygiene. None is security.

## Verified independently vs. taken on faith

**Verified in `/tmp/warden-lqb` (scratch copy; `npm ci` → 52 packages):**

- **`fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit` run in full and green** — Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (44 files, no fixes), Vitest (**8 files, 52 tests, all passing**), ShellCheck 0.11.0 (confirmed installed, so the step ran rather than short-circuiting). This matches the handoff's claim exactly, and unlike my predecessor at `fortkit-etr` I was able to reproduce every step rather than only Vitest.
- **Provenance of what I tested** — `/tmp/warden-lqb/src` and `/tmp/warden-lqb/test` are byte-identical to the `bead/lqb` worktree (`diff -rq`, no output), and that worktree is clean at `e77c365`.
- **Test-count monotonicity** — the diff adds one `test.each` with 3 cases and removes no `test(` declaration, so 49 → 52 is monotone with no assertion silently dropped. I read every removed line in both test files to confirm.
- **`detailIndex` equivalence** derived by hand for both branches of `visibleDetails`, including the overflow row and the past-the-end row.
- **Row-loop arithmetic** — row *i*'s baseline is `top + 46 + 13i`, ten pixels inside its own band `[top+36+13i, top+49+13i)`; the new loop's click points land where the code draws.
- **The stride change is a real layout change and it is safe** — workshops move from stride 265 to 245, so workshop *n* sits at `30 + 245n` (30/275/520/765 for four types, max extent 975 ≤ 1100). No overlap with the top row (y 35-147 vs 230-342) and none between neighbours (210 wide at 245 stride). Choosing 245 over 265 was the right pick — it keeps every existing top-row position, including the `765` the tests use, unchanged. Worth knowing that it does move workshops, which the handoff's "uses one `buildingStride` for every building row" does not say.
- **Fixture-name safety** — `Dorin Stoneward` / `Ari Vale` grep clean across `*.md`, `*.ts`, `*.json`, `*.jsonl`. **CSS specificity for finding 4** and the `esc()` → parser → serializer round-trip for finding 1 both worked through by hand.
- **Full read** of `src/colony-page.ts`, `src/colony-page.html`, both changed test files, the `colony-reader.ts` roster regexes (confirming the case-sensitivity claim the new `["Their", null]` case encodes), and my predecessor's complete round-1 verdict from the `fortkit-etr` bead record.

**Taken on faith:** nothing material. I could not read `/tmp/warden-etr.log` (outside my working directories), so my knowledge of round-1 findings 1 and 2 comes from the full verdict text stored on the `fortkit-etr` bead rather than from that log; the bead comment is complete and unabridged, so I do not think anything was lost. I did not run the suite against `main` to confirm 49 by execution — that number is inferred from the diff, and the 52 I measured is direct.

**Recommendation:** merge. File findings 1-7 as a follow-up bead sequenced before `fortkit-on6`, with finding 1 at the top — on6 reworks this exact surface, and a poll guard that silently doesn't fire is the kind of thing a rewrite inherits and never revisits.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: 6/6 criteria met, full verifier green (52 tests); 7 non-blocking, top: innerHTML guard defeated by apostrophes

I've read the charter, remember.md, and my seat file; pulled the diff; and reproduced the verifier in the scratch tree. Here is the review.

---

Warden review (Ilva Trueglass (she/her), opus): VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS

**Scope.** Single commit `d56bb5d` on `bead/994`, based on `47fcc89` (main has since moved to `7ffdc17` via the etr merge). Use `main...bead/994` — the two-dot range misleadingly shows etr's colony-page work as reverted. The real change set is 6 files: `src/ambient.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, `test/ambient.test.ts`, `test/cli.test.ts`, `docs/specs/ambient-life.md`, `fort/handoffs/forge-2026-08-07.md`.

**Model.** The handoff self-reports "GPT-5 Codex, as Kethra Anvilmark (she/her)" — a name that is not a rung on the charter's Forge ladder (GPT-5.6 Terra → Sol → Sonnet 5 → Opus 5). I applied the reward-hacking scrutiny the seat file asks for on that vendor: I specifically hunted for tautological tests and constants tuned to make an assertion pass. Findings 4 and 6 below are what that turned up. Neither is a fabricated pass — every new test does exercise a real, discriminating property — but they are the two places where the diff is thinner than it looks.

**Round one. Nothing here is blocking. All eight bead items are implemented and each is pinned by a test.** Item-by-item: (1) per-citizen favourite via `hash(identity) % 4` with a ~75/25 favourite/variety split ✓; (2) `--since` is now a true interval via `formatAmbientSince`, `--on` is the containing UTC day, both documented in the spec ✓; (3) `sharedWindow` jitters arrivals/departures around guaranteed cores ✓; (4) charter-regex seed replaced with a registry lookup that throws, `fortSeed` narrowed to `number` ✓; (5) `millisecondsAt` throws `RangeError` ✓; (6) `AmbientPlace` union declared and enforced through `pursuits` ✓; (7) the tautological DST test replaced with a `TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati` subprocess and an absolute expectation ✓; (8) CLI-level exit-code test added ✓.

---

### Findings

**1. (non-blocking) The meal jitter has one bit of entropy per citizen, and arrival and departure are structurally locked opposite.**

`sharedWindow` derives both offsets from `hash(...) % 2`. FNV-1a's bit 0 has no avalanche: the multiplier `0x01000193` is odd, so `low(a*prime) == low(a)`, and bit 0 of the digest reduces exactly to `1 XOR (parity of odd-valued charCodes in the input)`. Consequences, derived from the source rather than observed:

- `"arrival"` has odd-char parity 1 and `"departure"` parity 0, and the two strings share the entire `identity + name` prefix. So `approach` and `departure` **always differ**: a citizen is either (−30, +15) or (−15, +30), never (−15, +15) or (−30, +30). Two of the four intended jitter combinations never occur.
- `"lunch"` and `"dinner"` both have parity 0; `"breakfast"` and `"social"` both have parity 1. So each citizen's lunch and dinner jitter are identical, their breakfast and social jitter are identical, and the two groups are exact complements. One bit governs the whole day.
- The jitter hash has no day term, so a citizen's arrival time is the same every day forever.

The acceptance criterion is met literally (citizens do differ from each other, and the cores are guaranteed — I checked that sleep can never eat a core: latest wake is 07:00 vs. breakfast core 07:15, earliest sleep 21:00 vs. social core ending 20:30). But the fort breathes in two fixed cohorts rather than continuously, and that is not what "jitter arrivals/departures so the fort breathes" was after. The fix is one token — take higher bits (`(hash(...) >>> 8) % 3` or similar) and add a day term. File as a bead.

**2. (non-blocking) `formatAmbientWindow` iterates the whole interval quarter-hour by quarter-hour, unbounded.**

`fortkit ambient kethra --since 1970-01-01` walks ~2M quarter-hours; `--since 0001-01-01` walks ~71M and accumulates millions of merged spans. It degrades to slow, never to wrong, and it is bounded above by `now − since`, so this is threat-model class 1 (agent accident — a wrong `--since`) at low cost. Worth a cap or a chunked render. Also: for windows longer than a day the output is bare `HH:MM–HH:MM` lines with no date, so a multi-day `--since` renders repeating clock times that a reader cannot disambiguate. Bead.

**3. (non-blocking, and the one I'd act on before fci.6) The registry lookup will reject the very callers fci.6 is meant to serve.**

`currentFortName` matches `cwd === path || cwd.startsWith(path + sep)` against registry entries. The `+ sep` guard is exactly right — it correctly refuses to match `/home/justin/dev/fortkit-worktrees/994` against a registered `/home/justin/dev/fortkit`, avoiding the sibling-prefix bug. But that correctness *is* the problem for the launcher: the Forge runs in a worktree and the Warden runs in a `/tmp` scratch copy, and worktrees are tracked as benches inside a fort's projection, not as registered forts. So `fortkit ambient` exits 1 from a seat's actual cwd. Two lesser edges land in the same place: a future `--since` (clock skew on a session-start timestamp) raises `RangeError`, and a registry entry with a trailing slash or a `..` never matches, because `readRegistry` returns absolute paths un-`resolve`d.

This is not a regression — the bead asked for "registry or fail loudly" and loud is what it got — and I could not read `~/.claude/civilization.json` to confirm the worktree paths are absent, so treat that as inference from `readers/registry.ts` and the colony projection shape. But bead 994 exists precisely to settle this surface *before* fci.6 builds on it, so fci.6 should be told now: it needs a fort-name resolution that survives worktrees (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, or an explicit `--fort` argument), not a rediscovery in the launcher. Bead.

**4. (non-blocking) The pursuit table's order is tuned to a coincidence, and the spec states the coincidence as a general property.**

`// Keep fishing last: Kethra's identity hash selects it as her favourite` makes array order load-bearing on `hash("<Manyhalls seed>\0kethra") % 4 == 3`. Rename the fort and Kethra stops fishing; add a fifth pastime and the test breaks. The underlying mechanism (per-citizen hash favourite) is principled and is what the bead asked for, the tuning is disclosed rather than hidden, and the test does pin it — so this is honest, not a fabricated pass. But the spec now says flatly "Each citizen deterministically favours one pastime (Kethra favours fishing)", with no note that this holds for one fort's seed. This spec is read by settlements that do not exist yet. One qualifying clause fixes it. Bead.

**5. (non-blocking) `river` and `tinker-bench` were deleted rather than declared, so fishing now happens at the walls.**

Finding 6 asked for a union so a typo becomes a type error, aligned with the layout table. The union is real and does catch typos (`home:${string}` correctly covers homes). But the alignment was achieved by relabelling: `["fishing", "river"]` → `["fishing", "walls"]` and `["tinkering", "tinker-bench"]` → `["tinkering", "archive"]`, collapsing four pursuits onto two places. "fishing at walls" is the kind of line that renders beautifully and reads wrong, and it will render in fci.6's session-start line.

I also checked the claim of alignment against the actual table: `buildingLayouts` on main is `gate / depot / archive / dungeon / workshop` — **`tavern` and `walls` appear in no layout table either.** So the original complaint ("exist in no layout table") is half-addressed. I do not call this a false record: `docs/specs/ambient-life.md:51` independently defines the ambient vocabulary as "home:<citizen>, tavern, archive, walls, ...", `buildingLayouts` is the world/colony *bead-and-bench* renderer rather than the L4 sprite layout, and the handoff flags the relabel as an open risk. But declaring the destinations and letting L1/L4 add them would have been the better call than moving the fisherman to the ramparts. Bead, for L1/L4 to reconcile; the trailing "..." on spec line 51 now overstates the union and should go.

**6. (non-blocking) Two of the new assertions carry no information beyond exit status.**

`expect(stdout).toBe("")` in the TZ test asserts that a child which prints nothing printed nothing; the real check is that `execFileAsync` did not reject, because the child calls `process.exit(1)` on mismatch. Likewise the CLI success path asserts `resolves.toEqual(expect.anything())`, which matches any `{stdout, stderr}`. Both tests do work — I traced the TZ one and it is genuinely discriminating (Pacific/Kiritimati is UTC+14, so a local-time implementation would read 12:30Z as 02:30 and return `sleeping`, not `lunching`) — and item 8 asked for an exit-code test, which is what this is. But a failure yields no diagnostic, and given item 7 was itself about a test that could not fail, the shape deserves naming. Moving the comparison into the parent (print JSON, assert on it) costs nothing. Bead.

**7. (non-blocking) The acceptance clause "suite green under a non-UTC TZ in CI fashion" is met by one stubbed test, not by CI.**

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets no `TZ`, and GitHub runners are UTC, so in CI exactly one test runs under a non-UTC zone. The whole-suite property holds today — I verified it myself under `TZ=America/Anchorage` — but nothing pins it. A one-line `env: TZ: America/Anchorage` on the verify job closes it. Per standing order 5, that config recommendation gets its own follow-up bead verifying it was applied.

**8. (non-blocking) Unregistered-fort failure exits 1 via an unhandled top-level rejection, printing a stack trace.**

Loud, which is what was asked, and the new test pins the code. But the neighbours use exit 2 with a clean `console.error`, and a stack trace is a poor thing to inject into a session-start line. Catch and `console.error` + `process.exitCode = 1`. Bead.

**9. (non-blocking, unresolved) I could not reproduce the handoff's `execFile` claim.**

The "Failed attempts" section states "This environment's `execFile` suppresses stdout for successful positional Node scripts", and that diagnosis shaped the test design in finding 6. `test/git.test.ts` captures subprocess stdout from `git` without trouble, and Node's `--eval` writes to stdout normally, so I suspect a misdiagnosis of something else. I could not check: direct `node` invocation is outside my permission set. I am not calling this a falsified record — it sits in a Failed-attempts section describing the author's own experience — but it should not be carried forward as an established environment fact.

---

### Verified independently

- Installed deps in the scratch tree (`npm ci`) and ran `CI=1 TZ=America/Anchorage fort/scripts/verify.sh --no-emit`: **green** through Node typecheck, browser typecheck, Biome (44 files), Vitest, and ShellCheck. This confirms the handoff's "52 tests across 8 files" and its `TZ=America/Anchorage` claim.
- `npm test -- --reporter=verbose`: all 52 named tests pass, including the five new ambient tests and the new CLI exit-code test.
- Read the full post-change `src/ambient.ts` and `src/cli.ts`. Traced the argument validator by hand against flag-swap, duplicate-flag, both-flags, misplaced-flag, and citizen-named-`--on` cases — all correctly rejected.
- Traced `formatAmbientWindow`'s sampling for soundness: every transition boundary in the model (sleep at :00/:30, cores at :15/:45, jitter in 15-minute steps, pursuit blocks at 3-hour marks) is a multiple of 15 minutes, so quarter-hour sampling cannot skip a state, and the partial first/last spans are correct.
- Derived the FNV-1a bit-0 property in finding 1 from the source; confirmed the odd-char parities of `"arrival"`/`"departure"` and of the four window names by hand.
- Confirmed `buildingLayouts` on main (`git show main:src/colony-page.ts`) contains no `tavern` and no `walls`.
- Confirmed `readRegistry`'s `fort_name`/`repo` schema matches the CLI test's fixture, and that absolute registry paths are not re-`resolve`d.
- Confirmed the change set is disjoint from main's etr commits, so the merge into `7ffdc17` is clean despite the stale base.
- Confirmed no caller of `activity`/`formatAmbientDay` exists outside `ambient.ts` and `cli.ts`, and that no launcher invokes `fortkit ambient` — so narrowing `fortSeed` to `number` and redefining `--since` break nothing today. Item 2's "fix it before fci.6 makes it a breaking change to a gate-1 caller" is satisfied.
- Gate check: the diff touches `fort/handoffs/` only, which is seat-writable working record, not `fort/charter.md`, `fort/seats/`, `fort/profiles/`, or a launcher. No human-gate-1 trigger, no auth surface, no data-mutating migration. No ESCALATE.

### Taken on faith

- The contents of `~/.claude/civilization.json` (not readable from this seat), so finding 3's worktree claim is inference from `readers/registry.ts` and the colony projection, not observation.
- The handoff's `execFile` claim (finding 9) and its self-reported model identity.
- I could not execute `node` directly, so behavioural spot-checks beyond the test suite — sampling the favourite distribution, eyeballing rendered output — were done by reading and derivation rather than by running.

Nothing above meets the bar of making the fort worse than not merging. Findings 1–9 belong in beads; findings 3 and 5 should land before fci.5/fci.6 consume this surface, and finding 7 carries a standing-order-5 follow-up.

VERDICT-LINE: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS: all 8 items landed, verifier green under non-UTC TZ; 9 non-blocking findings, none worse than not merging

(5) The asset contract's master->runtime relation reads as a 2x downsample, contradicting the doc's own correct criticism of downsampling; state explicitly that the master is the native pixel grid and the runtime cell is world units at zoom 1, and forbid resampling the master.
